title: 01 - Pirates of Drinax
content: The Letter of Marque and the Legacy of Sindal PCs present Fomega (Scout/Mechanic/Medic): A tall and strong man, wears a wool hat and has a goatee. Seems to have memory problems. Jane (Rocío): Ex-military. Tall and strong, redhead (dyed), wears cargo pants and a rifle on her back. Nemo (James Nando): Noble/Ex-marine. A tall man, with long hair in a ponytail and a blue-dyed beard. Uses makeup and elegant suits to hide his age. Emilio: Noble/Astronavigator. A good-looking man, with a firm posture that denotes nobility and military training. Pika (Paloma): Pilot. A small woman of Asian features, tanned skin and a shaved head with black painted eyes. She is antisocial and only eats processed food. Jimmy Mendoza: Soldier. A man of athletic build, wiry, tanned skin, and a large American-style mustache. NPCs present Saldancet (Independent Merchant): The captain who transported the PCs to Drinax. Bri Tolar (Hawk Guard): Sergeant of the guard, wears a Battle Dress armor. Has minor noble titles (Viscountess, etc.). King Oleb XVI (King of Drinax): A huge, bombastic man who is fond of wine. A dreamer with airs of grandeur, he seeks to restore the empire. Princess Rao (Heir of Drinax): Young, intelligent, and pragmatic. She is the brains behind the clandestine operation. Lord Drax (Admiral of the Star Guard): Loyal to the king, in charge of the system's defense and custodian of the ship. Important Developments in the PJs' Lives or the Campaign The characters have accepted a Letter of Marque from King Oleb XVI, officially becoming privateers (pirates) in the secret service of Drinax.    The long-term goal is to destabilize trade in the Trojan Reach* to force independent systems to seek Drinax's protection, thus rebuilding the ancient Sindal Empire. The group has taken possession of a Harrier-class Trade Incursor, a high-tech but very old ship, which will serve as their base of operations. Loose Ends The ship requires continuous repairs; although functional, the hull is damaged (56/88 points) and systems consume double energy until fully tuned. Nemo has a personal vendetta against his nephew, whom he wants dead to secure his noble title. The ship's name has not been fully formalized, though "Banshee" is the favorite. The crew must keep their affiliation with Drinax absolutely secret, or the Imperium or the Aslan will retaliate. Scene 1: Arrival at the Floating Palace PCs present: All. NPCs present: Saldancet (Merchant), Bri Tolar (Hawk Guard, Sergeant in power armor). Location: Cargo Docks (Floating Palace / Drinax). Ships: Saldancet's Ship (Merchant Freighter, Captain Saldancet). The group arrives at the planet Drinax, a world devastated by the Aslan two centuries ago. They land at the Floating Palace, a magnificent baroque structure that hovers above the radioactive surface thanks to antigravity technology. Captain Saldancet drops them off at the docks, where they are met by Sergeant Bri Tolar of the Hawk Guard. Their weapons and armor are confiscated for security before the royal audience. While being escorted through service tunnels (to maintain their presence secret), the characters observe the contrast between the palace's priceless works of art and the functional poverty of its inhabitants, who use ancient relics for mundane tasks. Scene 2: The Dragon King's Offer PCs present: All. NPCs present: King Oleb XVI (King of Drinax, bombastic, drinker, archetype of "The Bombastic King"), Princess Rao (Heiress, young, shrewd, archetype of "The Mastermind"). Location: Throne Room (Floating Palace / Drinax). The characters are brought before King Oleb in the Throne Room, presided over by the Dragon Throne, made from the wreckage of defeated starships. Oleb, with a goblet of wine in hand and great enthusiasm, reveals his master plan: to restore the glory of the Kingdom of Drinax. He offers them a "gem" from the ancient Sindal Empire: a Harrier warship. In exchange, he delivers a digitally signed Letter of Marque. Their orders are to attack stellar trade (both Imperial and Aslan) to "bleed them dry" until neighboring worlds beg for Drinax's protection. The conditions are clear: 1.  10% of the loot goes to the King. 2.  They must maintain Drinax's involvement in absolute secrecy. 3.  They must win hearts and minds in border worlds, not just steal. 4.  If successful, they will receive noble titles and lands. Princess Rao appears to add a dose of reality and pragmatism to her father's plan, suggesting that political marriage with one of the PCs could be a future reward. Scene 3: Inspection and Repair of the Harrier PCs present: All. NPCs present: Lord Drax (Admiral, loyal, archetype of "The Old Military"). Location: Drinax Orbit (Gas Giant Moon / Drinax System). Ships: Harrier (Sindalian Trade Incursor, No Captain assigned yet). Lord Drax escorts the characters to a distant moon where the ship is hidden. The Harrier is a Tech Level 15 ship, with advanced capabilities like stealth jumps and particle weaponry, but it is in a state of evident deterioration after centuries of abandonment or misuse. The interior is luxurious, paneled in wood and decorated with bas-reliefs, but functionally touched. The characters (and players) spend time assessing the damage and spending their resources ("Ship Shares") to get it ready: Repair the missile turret to have a 360-degree firing arc. Stabilize the maneuver drive to prevent critical shutdowns. Improve general systems to reduce maintenance costs. Partially repair the hull (reaching 56 out of 88 health points). Invest in cosmetics to make the hull look intimidating (possibly painting a skull or symbol). Scene 4: Assignment of Roles and Quarters PCs present: All. NPCs present: None. Location: Ship Deck (Harrier / Drinax System). Ships: Harrier (Sindalian Trade Incursor, Captain Nemo). After the repairs, the group discusses the ship's hierarchy and distribution. Captain: It is agreed that Nemo will be captain due to his social status and experience. Officers: It is established that key roles (Pilot, Engineer, Gunner, Astrogator/Communications) will have officer rank. Second in Command: Pika (Paloma) is designated as second in command/Commodore, despite her antisocial nature, to manage the ship while the captain sleeps. Accommodation: The four luxury officer cabins are assigned to the nobles and principal officers (Nemo, Emilio, Jane/Rocío). Pika, despite being an officer, prefers to sleep in a standard, dark, and isolated cabin, ceding her luxury spot to Fomega or Juan. The ship's name is debated, with "Banshee" being the strongest option, though it is not definitively closed. The session ends with the crew ready to seek their first loot and supplies, as they have no liquid cash or credits.

title: 01 - Welcome to Barovia
content: Session Title: The Fog's Threshold PCs present: Pulgar "Bigtoe" Ceres Broseph Lorna (Referred to as the druid/Dewdrop in the transcript) Renoir (The bard, played by Nacho) NPCs present: None physically present in real-time, but mentioned in flashbacks or references: Madame Eva, Durst Family, Stanimir (referred to as Estanimir/Talimira), Strahd. Locations: Barovia (The entrance road and gates). Main Events and Loose Ends The group spends a significant portion of the time reminiscing about who they were before arriving in these cursed lands, establishing their backgrounds and personal motivations. It is confirmed that they have leveled up after surviving the "House of Death" (Durst House), although they have emerged with mental and physical sequelae (Pulgar has aged 30 years and has a white streak). After being stripped of much of their equipment by the Vistani, they advance along the only possible westward path. The main landmark is crossing the Gates of Barovia; immense iron gates that open on their own as they pass and slam shut behind them with a deafening roar, leaving them trapped in the valley with Castle Ravenloft in the distance. Session Loose Ends Pulgar's Curse: The dwarf has magically aged 30 years. It is unknown if this is reversible or if it will have further consequences. The Shepherd Wolves: A pack of wolves has followed the group from the house to the gates without attacking, behaving like sheepdogs guiding a flock. Their exact purpose or who controls them is unknown. The Stolen Equipment: The Vistani stole Pulgar's amulet and much of the group's equipment after getting them drunk. Recovering their belongings remains a pending motivation. The Tarokka Deck: Renoir discovers he has the deck in his pocket, which now acts as his arcane focus. His connection to the destiny or magic of this place is yet to be explained. Session Joke During the tense inspection of the gigantic and ancient Gates of Barovia, which magically open without anyone pushing them, Pulgar breaks the atmosphere of terror with his dwarven pragmatism. While the others worry about dark magic or the decapitated heads of the statues, the dwarf complains about the "human manufacturing," criticizing the lack of a proper hydraulic system or decent levers, attributing the creaking and state of the gate to poor engineering rather than a supernatural curse. Scene 1: Echoes of a Former Life PCs present: Pulgar, Ceres, Broseph, Lorna, Renoir. NPCs present: Stanimir (Mentioned in flashback, Vistani leader, storyteller). Location: The road to Barovia (and flashbacks to the Vistani camp and Faerûn). Loot obtained: Tarokka Deck (Discovered in Renoir's pocket, functions as an arcane focus). Scene Summary: The DM prompts the players to recall their origins and how they arrived there. It is revealed that Pulgar is a jeweler turned thief seeking a stolen masterpiece; Lorna is a druid sold by her parents to a hermit; Ceres is a cleric of Chauntea who was burned alive and resurrected by her deity; and Broseph is a former guard from Waterdeep who fled after discovering a conspiracy. Renoir, the bard, has changed his stage name to "Renoir of the Forgotten" and has begun writing obsessively. The night with the Vistani is recalled, where Stanimir told the story of a cursed prince (Strahd) and how the Vistani have permission to enter and leave his lands, asking the adventurers to break their lord's curse. It is also mentioned that they possess the deeds to a mill. Scene 2: The Path of Wolves PCs present: Pulgar, Ceres, Broseph, Lorna, Renoir. NPCs present: None (Only local fauna). Location: A dark and muddy dirt road surrounded by a dense, foggy forest. Loot obtained: None. Scene Summary: The group travels for about five hours through an oppressive environment. The sky is leaden gray, there is a constant drizzle, and the sun is not visible. Broseph's passive perception and the others' instincts notice they are being followed by wolves. However, the animals do not attack; they stay at the edge of the forest, watching. Pulgar comments that they remind him of the sheepdogs from his homeland, suggesting they are guiding or "herding" them towards a specific destination rather than hunting them. The atmosphere is depressing and unnatural. Scene 3: The Gates of Desolation PCs present: Pulgar, Ceres, Broseph, Lorna, Renoir. NPCs present: None. (Statues of decapitated guardians - Archetype: Silent Guardians / Harbinger of Death). Location: The Gates of Barovia (Stone wall with rusted iron gates). Loot obtained: None. Scene Summary: The road ends at immense iron gates flanked by stone statues whose heads lie decapitated on the ground. As they approach, the gates creak and open on their own, inviting them to pass. Ceres tries to track footprints but finds no sign of recent human passage, only animals. Pulgar inspects the stone and metal, noting the antiquity and disrepair, although the gates show signs of recent use. The group, with no other option given that the fog behind them is impenetrable, crosses the threshold. As soon as they do, the gates slam shut violently behind them with a metallic roar. The fog momentarily dissipates to reveal the towers of Castle Ravenloft in the distance, confirming they have entered a prison from which they may not be able to escape.

title: 02 - Message in the Mud
content: Here is the session summary based on the provided transcript, following the requested format and in Spanish from Spain. Session: The Message in the Mud PCs present: Thumb "Bigtoe" Ceres Broseph Feyre Ladril Gabriel (Sir Gabriel) Hulio Renoir NPCs present: Pack of Dire Wolves (Giant/Terrible Wolves) Corpse of the messenger from Barovia Major events and loose ends: The group ventures into the forests of Barovia after being transported by fog after interacting with some Vistani. They are ambushed by an unusually fierce pack of dire wolves. They find the corpse of a messenger with a letter from Burgomaster Kolian Indirovich desperately asking for help to save his love, Ireena Kolyana. Loose end: The group must reach the village of Barovia mentioned in the letter to claim the reward and understand what threatens Ireena. Unexplained loose ends from the session: The exact origin of the fog preventing them from retreating. The nature of the "curse" that fell upon the prince the Vistani spoke of (Strahd). Who the spectral rider was that Renoir mentions hearing/seeing before joining the combat. Session Joke: During combat, Sir Gabriel (Ladril) is gravely wounded. To use his Lay on Hands ability as a bonus action, he describes the action of "touching himself" to readjust his noble parts ("me toco mis cojones"), which causes laughter and approval from the table ("Guapísimo" - Very handsome/cool) for such a peculiar way of healing in the middle of battle. Scene 1: Memories in the Fog PCs present: Thumb, Ceres, Broseph, Feyre, Sir Gabriel, Hulio, Renoir. NPCs present: None (Mention of Vistani and Goblins in the flashback). Location: A road in a sinister and foggy forest of Barovia. Loot: None. Summary: The session begins with a recap of how the group arrived at their current situation. Originally mercenaries in Faerûn working for a countess, they recovered goods from some goblins and drove off some Vistani. After sharing a night with the Vistani and hearing the story of a cursed prince and a distant land, they awoke in Barovia: a place of thick fog, dark trees, and no sun. Each character is briefly introduced, highlighting their origins and how the transition to this place has affected them (premature aging in Thumb, natural discomfort in Ceres, noble stoicism in Sir Gabriel, recent traumas in Renoir). The group advances along the road, noting that the fog prevents them from seeing the treetops and the road seems like the only safe option. Scene 2: The Ambush at the Puddle PCs present: Thumb, Ceres, Broseph, Feyre, Sir Gabriel, Hulio, Renoir (joins at the end). NPCs present: Dire Wolves: (Beasts, Predators) Pony-sized wolves with grayish/white fur, covered in mud, possessing unnatural ferocity. Brown Bear: (Beast, Wild Shape) Feyre's transformation for combat. Location: A clearing in the forest near the road, around a puddle of black water and mud. Loot: Wolf meat (of questionable culinary quality). Summary: The group perceives a strong smell of rot. Upon investigating off the road, they find a half-submerged corpse in a puddle of black water. Before they can examine it closely, they are ambushed by five dire wolves lurking among the trees. A chaotic combat ensues. Feyre transforms into a brown bear to protect the flank. Hulio is knocked down by the wolves but recovers. Sir Gabriel tanks with a dagger (and then a rusty sword) and heals himself by readjusting "his attributes." Thumb lands a devastating critical sneak attack. Renoir dramatically appears from the fog (after being absent updating his character sheet) and lands a final critical blow with his rapier. The group manages to take down the pack, though they suffer several injuries. Scene 3: The Last Message PCs present: Thumb, Ceres, Broseph, Feyre, Sir Gabriel, Hulio, Renoir. NPCs present: The Messenger (Corpse): (Victim) A commoner human who died approximately a week ago, partially devoured by the wolves. Location: The same black water puddle in the forest. Loot: Letter from Kolian Indirovich. Rusty longsword (equipped by Sir Gabriel). Cloak of Protection (won by Feyre after a dice roll). Blacksmithing equipment and chain mail (assigned to Hulio). Summary: After the combat, Ceres heals the group with a prayer to Chauntea. They examine the corpse in the puddle, confirming it died from the wolves' attack. In his pouch, they find a sealed and slightly wet letter written by Kolian Indirovich, the Burgomaster. The letter is a desperate plea for help to save his love, Ireena Kolyana, from a deadly threat, promising his entire fortune in return. They also recover a rusty longsword from the mud, which Sir Gabriel claims. Thumb organizes a "fair" raffle (by rolling d20s) to distribute a Cloak of Protection found (apparently carried over from a previous session or common pool loot). Feyre wins the cloak. Finally, the group dismembers the wolves for meat, though the quality of the cut leaves much to be desired, and they decide to bury the messenger under some stones before continuing their journey to the village.

title: 02 - Pirates of Drinax
content: Here is the session summary in the requested format, using Spanish from Spain. The Banshee and the First Steps PCs present: Nemo, Paloma, Pika (Jane), Juan's Character (Yankee/Soldier), Álvaro's Character (mentioned). NPCs present: Lord Wrax (Admiral of the Star Guard), King Oleb XVI (mentioned), Princess Rao (mentioned), Sal Danczo (mentioned). Main developments in the PCs' lives or in the campaign:    The group officially takes possession of their ship, a Harrier*-class raider, to begin their privateer mission in the service of the Kingdom of Drinax. The command hierarchy and the economic distribution of future loot are established, which is crucial for morale and the maintenance of the operation. The ship is christened Banshee. Loose ends: The pending meeting with Sal Danczo to obtain information and potential jobs. The hiring of additional crew and the purchase of supplies (including possible protocol or cleaning robots). The choice of the first concrete target to raid or investigate outside the Drinax system. Ship Delivery and Recognition PCs present: Nemo, Paloma, Pika, Juan's Character, Álvaro's Character. NPCs present: Lord Wrax (Admiral of the Star Guard, serious, reluctant to hand over the ship), King Oleb XVI (mentioned as the drunk patron). Location: Star Guard Hangar (Drinax). Ships: Banshee (Harrier Class, Tech Level 15), System defense ships (mentioned). Scene Summary: The Game Master describes the current situation. After accepting King Oleb XVI's offer, the characters are escorted by the Star Guard to their new ship. It is a ship of Sindalite design, technologically very advanced (TL 15), superior to what Drinax can currently produce. They meet Lord Wrax, who is unhappy to hand over such a valuable asset to some "mercenaries/privateers," but he obeys orders. It is explained that Drinax's fleet is scarce, mainly composed of defense ships without jump drives. The King has ordered them to get the ship operational and take it to port for inspection. The group begins to organize, choosing cabins; Nemo claims one of the best, while others settle for what's available. Officers' Meeting: Hierarchy and Wine PCs present: Nemo, Paloma, Pika, Juan's Character, Álvaro's Character. NPCs present: None. Location: Command Bridge / Officers' Lounge (The Banshee). Ships: Banshee. Scene Summary: Nemo calls a meeting on the bridge, assuming the role of Captain and toasting with a bottle of wine (possibly found on the ship). The immediate plan of action is discussed. Nemo suggests raiding a small merchant ship to test the systems and coordinate. Paloma proposes searching for trade routes. Pika suggests contacting Sal Danczo, the smuggler who brought them, as she might have information about vulnerable enemies or rivals, which would be a good starting point for making "friends" at home. They agree to dock at Drinax, make purchases, and then depart. The Division of Booty and Logistics PCs present: Nemo, Paloma, Pika, Juan's Character. NPCs present: None. Location: The Banshee (Drinax). Ships: Banshee. Scene Summary: An intense discussion takes place regarding the ship's finances. It is agreed that 10% of the loot goes to King Oleb. Of the remainder, Nemo proposes setting aside 50% for the ship's fund (repairs and maintenance). The dispute arises over the distribution of the remainder: the pirate norm is usually 5 parts for the captain, 2 for officers, and 1 for the crew. Juan's character opposes the captain earning so much ("Socialism" vs. military ranks). After a debate, Nemo agrees to lower his share to 4 to calm things down. The cost of maintaining each character's living standard (Social Standing) is also discussed. Pika expresses her desire to buy protocol and cleaning robots, but the catalog prices (from 350,000 to millions of credits) are prohibitive for now. Christening and Final Planning PCs present: Nemo, Paloma, Pika, Juan's Character. NPCs present: Sal Danczo (mentioned as a contact). Location: The Banshee (Drinax). Ships: Banshee. Scene Summary: Finally, the ship's name is confirmed: Banshee, in the absence of a better proposal. Paloma's idea of going to search for Sindalite ruins immediately is discarded, as the GM clarifies that it would require a lot of time and specialized archaeological knowledge, and is not as simple as finding treasure in plain sight. The group decides that their immediate priority is to obtain information (investigate targets) and undertake small jobs to earn money and better equip the ship before facing the Empire or larger objectives. The plan is to go see Sal Danczo at the palace.

title: 03 - PoD - Honour Among Thieves 01
content: Here is the session summary following the requested format: Session Title: The Pirate Lady and the Torpol Trail PCs Present Captain Nemo, Jimmy, Emilio, Paloma, Rocío, Fomega. NPCs Present Princess Rao, King Oleb XVI, Margaret Blaine, Provost Falx. Major Developments Campaign Strategy: The roadmap for Drinax's reconstruction has been defined: carry out "false flag" attacks on trade (especially GeDeCo and the Hierate) to destabilize the region and subsequently offer protection under the banner of Drinax.    New Ally: Margaret Blaine, the legendary pirate, has temporarily joined the crew of the Banshee* with the objective of reaching the Marduk system.    Darokin's Trail: A direct connection has been discovered between the pirate attacks in Torpol and Admiral Darokin's fleet (via the ship Mercifuge*). Loose Ends The Scout Ship: A Scout-type ship has been detected in the lower port of Torpol which received an encrypted signal from the pirates. Its crew and purpose remain an unknown that must be investigated. The Fate of the Chemicals: It is not known where the pirates plan to sell the stolen chemicals from the refinery.    The Cicentai*: Margaret Blaine's personal mission to recover her belongings from her former ship in Marduk remains pending. Scene 1: Strategy and Geopolitics PCs Present: All. NPCs Present: Princess Rao (Pragmatic strategist, Archetype: The Mastermind). Location: Royal Palace (Drinax/Drinax System). Ships Mentioned: None. Scene Summary: The crew meets with Princess Rao to discuss the political situation of the Cluster. The resentment of worlds like Clarke towards Drinax and the growing influence of the GeDeCo corporation, especially in Borite, is revealed. The strategy of attacking trade without officially involving the Kingdom, using intermediaries for the sale of loot, is agreed upon. Rao informs about a reward of 2.5 million credits for the pirates operating in Clarke and Torpol. Scene 2: Dinner with the Legend PCs Present: All. NPCs Present: King Oleb XVI (Boisterous and jovial ruler, Archetype: The Warrior/Jester King), Margaret Blaine (Refined and quiet elder, Archetype: The Mentor/Old Guard). Location: Royal Dining Room (Drinax/Drinax System). Ships Mentioned: Cicentai (Unknown Model, Unknown Captain - Blaine's former ship). Scene Summary: During a royal dinner, King Oleb introduces Margaret Blaine, a retired pirate of great renown. Blaine agrees to join the journey to recover personal items from the Cicentai in Marduk. During the evening, she offers valuable advice to the crew on the importance of discretion, changing identities, and maintaining an information network, advising against hiring external crew for the time being. Scene 3: Jump into the Void PCs Present: All. NPCs Present: Margaret Blaine. Location: Deep Space and Jump Space (Between Drinax and Torpol). Ships Mentioned: Banshee (Harrier Class, Captain Nemo). Scene Summary: The crew executes departure maneuvers. Emilio and Paloma successfully manage astrogation and the jump. During the week of transit in hyperspace, Margaret Blaine shares stories of her past and suggests conducting combat drills, noting that the crew could benefit from refining their combat tactics. Scene 4: Investigation in Paradise PCs Present: All (Paloma and Fomega performing technical analysis). NPCs Present: Provost Falx (Wears exotic local fashion, Archetype: The Grateful Bureaucrat). Location: Polar Resort and Government Building (Torpol/Torpol System). Ships Mentioned: Argo 1 (Far Trader, Unknown Captain), Argo 2 (Salvage Hauler - Vulture Class, Unknown Captain), Mercifuge (Real name of Argo 2, Darokin Fleet), Scout (Exploration Ship, Unknown Captain). Scene Summary: Upon arriving at the water world of Torpol, the crew interviews Provost Falx and analyzes data from the refinery attack. They discover that the attackers used two ships: a Far Trader and a Salvage Hauler. Sensors reveal that the Hauler is actually the Mercifuge, a ship linked to the pirate Admiral Darokin, concealing its imperial insignias with fresh paint. Additionally, they intercept a communications trail linking the attackers to a mysterious Scout ship docked in the lower port. Scene 5: The Captain's Party PCs Present: All. NPCs Present: Tourists and locals (Archetype: Background extras). Location: Resort on an artificial island (Torpol/Torpol System). Ships Mentioned: None. Scene Summary: Captain Nemo organizes and funds a lavish party at the resort to lift the crew's morale and solidify their alibi as wealthy travelers. While the team enjoys the event, plans are being made to investigate the Scout ship identified in the previous scene.

title: 03 - Welcome to Barovia Blood and Silence
url: /en/ravenloft/03 - Welcome to Barovia Blood and Silence
content: Welcome to Barovia: Blood and Silence PCs present: Broseph, Ceres, Feyre, Sir Gabriel (Ladril), Hulio, Renoir (played by Nacho). NPCs present: Biltrad (Merchant), Parry (Merchant's assistant), Arik (Innkeeper), Three Vistani women, Ismark Kolyanovich (Ismark "the Younger"), Ireena Kolyana. Main Developments and Loose Ends: The group has finally arrived in the village of Barovia, finding a grim place with perpetual fog and terrified inhabitants who are barricading themselves in their homes. They managed to obtain provisions at exorbitant prices and met Ismark, the son of the recently deceased Burgomaster. Ismark revealed that the vampire Strahd is obsessed with his adopted sister, Ireena, whom he has already bitten twice. The group has agreed to help Ismark take his father's body to the church for burial and then escort Ireena to the walled city of Vallaki for her safety. Loose Ends from the Session: Mari's Crying: A woman named Mari is heard crying inconsolably in a house near the square, but the group has not investigated the exact cause or interacted with her. Madame Eva's Prophecy: The Vistani women at the inn have indicated to Renoir that he possesses a "gift of premonition" and urged him to visit Madame Eva at the gypsy camp (near Tser Pools) to learn more about his destiny. The Burial: The group plans to bury the Burgomaster at dawn before leaving for Vallaki. Session Joke: Broseph (Juan Casanova) repeatedly tries to make a pun with the name of the inn, calling it "Weak Blood" instead of "Blood of the Vine." When he finally tells the joke to Arik, the innkeeper ("Bloodless blood... Weak blood"), Arik looks at him with complete indifference, not understanding the joke and simply asking if he wants a pitcher or a glass, creating a moment of comedic awkwardness due to the Barovians' lack of humor. Scene 1: Shadows on the Road PCs present: All. NPCs present: None. Location: The forests on the outskirts of the village and the main road. Loot: None. Summary: After dealing with a corpse found in the forest and deciding not to take a short rest, the group advances through the fog. Feyre (in bear form) accompanies the group while Broseph comments on the strangeness of bringing a bear to a town. As they move west, the forest opens into a clearing, and they glimpse the first buildings with strange and grim architecture. Night falls as they enter the village of Barovia. Scene 2: The Ghost Town PCs present: All. NPCs present: Anonymous Villager (fleeing). Location: Streets of the village of Barovia. Loot: None. Summary: The group enters a silent, fog-covered village. They observe that many houses are barricaded from the outside and have claw marks (some from wolves, others from humanoids) on doors and walls. Cries of a woman are heard in the distance. Broseph tries to talk to a villager who hurries into his house, but he is ignored, and the door slams shut in his face. Renoir tries to play the violin to attract attention, but only succeeds in intensifying the woman's crying momentarily. Scene 3: Business at Biltrad's Provisions PCs present: All. NPCs present: Biltrad (Merchant, middle-aged man, broken face, unfriendly), Parry (Young assistant in leather armor). Location: "Biltrad's Provisions" shop, in the village square. Loot: 10 travel rations (Purchased in exchange for 2 gold rings). Summary: The group goes to the only open shop, knocking until they are let in. Biltrad, the owner, is reluctant to sell and warns that there are no travelers in Barovia. He sells his merchandise at ten times the normal price, claiming that "he is the market." Broseph negotiates by giving two gold rings in exchange for 10 travel rations, given the group's concern about the lack of supplies and their inability to hunt in an unknown environment. Scene 4: The "Blood of the Vine" Inn PCs present: All. NPCs present: Arik (Innkeeper, man of few words, indifferent), Three Vistani women (Owners, adult, mysterious), Ismark "the Younger" (Noble, tired but well-dressed, "Desperate Ally" archetype). Location: Inn in the village square. Loot: Information about Madame Eva. Summary: The group enters the inn, a run-down place. Renoir tells a story to the Vistani owners, who, pleased, reveal that he must seek out Madame Eva to understand his gift of premonition. Meanwhile, the rest of the group sits with Ismark, who was drinking alone. Ismark reveals that he is the son of the Burgomaster, who died two days ago due to Strahd's siege. The vampire is obsessed with his sister, Ireena, and the village is no longer safe. Ismark asks for help burying his father and getting his sister out of there. Scene 5: The Burgomaster's Mansion PCs present: All. NPCs present: Ireena Kolyana (Young noblewoman, beautiful, armed and in chain mail, "Warrior Damsel" archetype), Burgomaster's Corpse. Location: Kolyana family mansion, south of the village. Loot: None (the house has been stripped of value). Summary: The group accompanies Ismark to his mansion, which shows signs of siege (claw marks, burns, boarded-up windows). Ireena receives them with sword in hand, suspicious, until Ismark calms her. Inside, the group sees the Burgomaster's makeshift coffin. Ireena confirms that Strahd has bitten her twice and that he has some mental control over her, making her invite him in. The group debates whether to leave immediately or wait for the burial; they finally agree to spend the night in the mansion, help with the burial at dawn in Father Donavich's church, and then depart for Vallaki. Broseph searches for valuables or diaries unsuccessfully, while Ceres prays for the deceased.
snippet: Welcome to Barovia: Blood and Silence PCs present: Broseph, Ceres, Feyre, Sir Gabriel (Ladril), Hulio, Renoir (played by Nacho). NPCs present: Biltrad (Merchant), Parry (Merchant's assistant), Arik (Innkeeper), Three Vistani women, Ismark Kolyanovich (Ismark "the Younger"), Ireena Kolyana. Main Deve

title: 04 - PoD - Honour Among Thieves 02
content: Session Title: Clues in Paradise and the Jump to Borite PJs present: Nemo (Captain) Juan "Jimmy" (Security/Investigator) Paloma "Honor" (Merchant/Broker) Rocío "Taya" (Engineer/Pilot) Emilio "Pika" (Sensors/Astrographer) NPCs present: Provost Shala (Local leader in Torpol) Provost's Secretary Captain Daniel Blau (Merchant captain) Holmer (Scrap dealer) Lady Hil / Captain Blaine (Mentor on the ship) Important developments in the PJs' lives or the campaign: The crew has obtained a potential new mission ("side quest") from the Torpol authorities to steal technology on the planet Talhasa, which would improve diplomatic relations between Torpol and the Kingdom of Drinax. It has been confirmed that the target of their current pursuit (the vargr pirate Captain Krrsh/Crash) has fled towards the Borite system.  The PJs' ship, the Harrier* (Banshee), has suffered structural damage and a critical hit to the jump drive due to a risky refueling maneuver. Loose ends / Pending items: The Talhasa mission: Provost Shala has requested the kidnapping of Doctor Torcan and the theft of seeds from a floating biological facility. It remains to be decided when to carry it out. Repairs: The ship has hull damage and a critical issue with the jump drive that require costly repairs (spare parts) and time. Origin of the scrap: Krrsh sold old but highly selected computer components. It is unknown where he obtained them. Scene 1: Bureaucracy and Bribes PJs present: Nemo, Pika, Juan, Paloma. NPCs present: Spaceport officials (Bureaucrats). Location: Administrative offices and Police Station (Planet Torpol). Ships mentioned: Miseries Company (Scout, Captain Krrsh/Crash), Sarcomond (Far Trader Merchant, Captain Daniel Blau). Scene summary: Nemo and Pika attempt to arrange a meeting with a Provost through official channels and diplomacy, but fail miserably, losing two days in bureaucratic procedures. In parallel, Juan and Paloma go to the administration. Juan bribes an official with 500 credits (plus help from Paloma) to access the records. They discover that the ship they are looking for is the Miseries Company, captained by a vargr named Krrsh (or Crash). They learn that he sold computer scrap to a merchant named Holmer and had an armed confrontation with the ship Sarcomond before fleeing. Scene 2: Orbital Maintenance PJs present: Rocío. NPCs present: Lady Hil / Captain Blaine (Veteran pirate mentor). Location: Aboard the Banshee (Torpol orbital spaceport). Ships mentioned: Banshee (Harrier, Captain Nemo). Scene summary: While the rest of the group is on the surface, Rocío remains on the ship performing maintenance and cleaning tasks. She takes the opportunity to chat with Captain Blaine, who tells her pirate stories and gives her advice. Rocío tries to coordinate with the group on the ground but gets bored waiting. Scene 3: Encounter with Captain Blau PJs present: Juan, Paloma, Nemo, Pika. NPCs present: Captain Daniel Blau (Gruff merchant captain, hates pirates and Drinaxians). Location: Sports bar in a Resort (Planet Torpol). Ships mentioned: Sarcomond (Far Trader, Captain Daniel Blau), Miseries Company (Scout, Captain Krrsh). Scene summary: Juan and Paloma locate Captain Blau watching a water polo match. After buying him a beer and using persuasion, Blau tells them that Krrsh tried to assault him, demanding his cargo. Blau, who had hidden turrets, returned fire and damaged the pirate ship. He heard Krrsh panic and order an emergency jump towards the Borite system. When Nemo and Pika arrive at the bar, Blau spits on the floor and curses the "Drinaxians," so Juan discreetly orders them to withdraw to avoid ruining their cover. Scene 4: An Indecent Proposition PJs present: Rocío. NPCs present: Provost Shala (Political leader, elegant and calculating), Provost's Secretary. Location: Luxury restaurant with panoramic views (Planet Torpol). Ships mentioned: None. Scene summary: Rocío receives a call on the ship summoning her to an urgent meeting. She goes down to the surface and meets Provost Shala at a luxurious breakfast. Shala, knowing they are Drinax agents, offers them a deal: if they carry out a covert mission on the planet Talhasa (Dispres/Sindal Sector) to steal genetic samples and kidnap the scientist Doctor Torcan from a floating base, Torpol will consider an alliance with King Oleb. Rocío agrees to relay the message to her captain. Shala sends them the target information. Scene 5: The Scrap Dealer Holmer PJs present: Juan, Paloma, Nemo (observing), Pika (observing). NPCs present: Holmer (Scrap dealer, short, bald, and fat). Location: Scrap warehouse (Planet Torpol). Ships mentioned: None. Scene summary: The group visits Holmer. Juan discreetly places a hidden microphone while Paloma negotiates the purchase of spare parts to gain his trust. Holmer confirms that Krrsh sold him a shipment of old but good condition computer parts. He mentions that the pirate was alone in his ship (unusual for a Scout) and seemed to be in a hurry. After a small additional bribe, Holmer shows them the merchandise, confirming that Krrsh is a petty thief who likely fled in fear. Scene 6: Disastrous Refueling and Jump PJs present: All. NPCs present: Lady Hil / Captain Blaine. Location: Gas Giant (Torpol System) and Deep Space. Ships mentioned: Banshee (Harrier, Captain Nemo). Scene summary: The group decides to depart immediately for Borite to pursue Krrsh. To save money, Nemo orders the refueling of unrefined fuel in a local gas giant instead of buying it. Paloma pilots the ship into the giant's atmosphere but fails a piloting roll. The Banshee suffers significant damage (10% of the hull) and receives a critical hit to the jump drive. Despite the damage and the unrefined fuel, Pika calculates the route and they manage to make the jump to the Borite system, where they hope to find the pirate and repair the ship.

title: 04 - The Burgomaster's Funeral and the Secret of the Church
url: /en/ravenloft/04 - The Burgomaster's Funeral and the Secret of the Church
content: Here is the translation of your text into English, without adding or inventing anything: Session Summary: The Burgomaster's Funeral and the Secret of the Church PCs present: Pulgar (Juan Casanova), Ceres (Paloma), Broseph (Juan Maldonado), Erdan (Marcos), Renoir (Nacho), Ladril Gabriel (Álvaro - mentioned/assumes role in the plan). NPCs present: Ismark, Ireena/Irina, Father Donavich, Doru (heard), Mari. Locations: Barovia (Burgomaster's Mansion, Church and Cemetery, Mari's House). Main Developments and Loose Ends The group managed to discover the horrors hidden in the apparent tranquility of the village of Barovia before officiating the Burgomaster's funeral. A master deception plan ("the switcheroo") was devised to safely get Ireena out of town, using Renoir dressed as a woman as bait for Strahd. They discovered that the local priest keeps his son, transformed into a vampiric spawn, locked in the church basement, and that a young woman named Gertruda has fled from her overprotective mother. Finally, the Burgomaster was buried and the group prepares to depart for Balaquia or the settlement of Santa Barovia. Session Loose Ends What will happen to Doru, the vampirized son of Priest Donavich, locked in the church basement and hungry? Where is Gertruda, Mari's daughter who escaped four nights ago? Who was the mysterious "man in black" who led the villagers (including Doru) in an assault against Castle Ravenloft over a year ago? What kind of toys does this "Blinsky" make? Will the plan to use Renoir disguised as Ireena to trick Strahd during the journey work? Session Gag "Paco Porras the Bard / Guppy Goldberg": At the beginning of the session, Nacho completely forgets which Tarokka cards he drew in his great prophetic reading from the previous session. Faced with the group's taunts about his "30-second memory" and his role in the group, Nacho accepts his fate and proclaims himself "Guppy Goldberg the Bard" or "Paco Porras the Bard" (referencing flamboyant Spanish television psychics), assuming the role of a mad seer and bard. Later, to cover up his forgetfulness, he invents a rather convenient "premonitory dream" to guide the group. Honorable mention to Pulgar's plan to put Ireena's panties on Renoir to use him as a decoy in the carriage. Scene Breakdown Scene 1: Preparations, Autopsies, and False Prophecies PCs present: Pulgar, Ceres, Erdan, Renoir. NPCs present: Ismark (Sturdy, muscular, noble movements, militarized and protective attitude - Archetype: The Loyal Son / Noble Warrior), Ireena (Angelic face, dressed entirely in mourning with a black veil, stubborn and dignified - Archetype: Tragic Damsel / Proud Noble). Location(s): Burgomaster's Mansion (Barovia). Loot obtained: None. Scene Summary: Erdan shares his ancient knowledge of vampires, explaining that they are creatures of darkness that heal quickly, drink blood, and cannot cross rivers. Pulgar proposes an unorthodox plan: the druid (in horse form) and the paladin will secretly take Ireena out, while the rest of the group goes in the carriage with Renoir disguised in Ireena's clothes to attract Strahd's ambushes. Erdan asks Ismark for permission to examine his father's corpse magically and medically. After a diplomatic intercession from Renoir, Ismark reluctantly agrees. Erdan detects no magic or poison, confirming that the death appears natural (perhaps from fright or stress). The next morning, Renoir (to cover up his forgotten cards) invents a prophetic "dream" about a blinding light protecting the innocent, urging the group to visit the priest before the funeral. Scene 2: Exploring the Church PCs present: Pulgar, Ceres, Erdan, Broseph. NPCs present: Donavich (Tired and broken voice praying - Archetype: Desperate Priest), Doru (Banging wood from the sub-basement, shouting distressed and hungry - Archetype: Hidden Monster). Location(s): Exterior and interior of the ruined church (Barovia). Loot obtained: None. Scene Summary: While Renoir accompanies Ismark to notify the neighbors of the funeral, the rest of the group proceeds to the church, which is half-ruined and has boarded-up windows. Pulgar, using his stealth, circles around and peers through the cracks of a window. He sees a destroyed chapel lit by candles and hears Father Donavich begging the god Lathander for the soul of "Doru." Suddenly, Pulgar hears loud banging coming from the sub-basement and a guttural voice screaming, "I'm hungry, Father!" Pulgar returns and informs the group, suspecting that the humans are hiding very dark things. Scene 3: Father Donavich's Secret PCs present: Pulgar, Ceres, Erdan, Broseph. NPCs present: Father Donavich (Man with dark circles under his eyes, dirty, disheveled, mentally broken, insane but harmless gaze - Archetype: Tragic Father / Blind Fanatic). Location(s): Chapel and church rooms (Barovia). Loot obtained: A book titled "The Sword of Truth, The Uses of Logic in War Against Diabolical Energies as Applied by the Inquisition of Ulmiz" (Looted by Pulgar). Scene Summary: Ceres picks the lock and uses Thaumaturgy to enter illuminated by an angelic halo, trying to comfort the priest. Erdan casts Detect Thoughts and perceives the man's madness and sadness. Donavich confesses that a year ago, a man in black led the village youths (including his 20-year-old son Doru) against Strahd's castle. They all died, but Doru returned as a monster that feeds on blood. Ceres tells him bluntly that his son is undead and that the only real help is to end his suffering. Terrified that his son will be killed, Donavich locks the basement trapdoor and refuses to feed or kill him, preferring to wait for a miracle from Lathander. Ceres manages to persuade him not to feed Doru while they seek another solution. As they discuss, Pulgar sneaks into the priest's office and steals a book about inquisitions and imps. Scene 4: Mari's Cry PCs present: Renoir. NPCs present: Mari (Distraught woman, clutching a creepy doll - Archetype: Enraged Mother / Tragic Villager). Location(s): Mari's House (Barovia). Loot obtained: None material (Information: "Blinsky" brand dolls). Scene Summary: Renoir, walking through the village, hears crying coming from a house. Finding the door locked, he forces his way in by climbing through a window to the second floor. There he finds Mari, a woman crying on the bed clutching a monstrous doll. Mari confesses that her daughter Gertruda, whom she had kept hidden from the village for 17 years to protect her, packed a bundle and fled four nights ago, stealing her key. The woman is convinced her daughter is dead or in Strahd's hands. Renoir investigates the room, confirming the young woman's premeditated escape. He also examines the doll, discovering a tag that reads: "If it isn't fun, it isn't a Blinsky", a famous local toy maker. Mari refuses to give him the doll as a clue, and Renoir leaves, taking notes of everything. Scene 5: The Burial and Departure PCs present: Pulgar, Ceres, Erdan, Renoir, Broseph. NPCs present: Ismark, Ireena, Father Donavich. Location(s): Barovia Cemetery. Loot obtained: Silvered short sword (Given by Ireena to Renoir). Scene Summary: The group reunites and carries the Burgomaster's coffin to the cemetery, accompanied by a few apathetic villagers. A somber ceremony is officiated where Ireena mourns her father's loss. Donavich, amazed by the presence of a dwarf and an elf (races he has only seen as ghosts marching towards Ravenloft), advises them on their journey: he recommends they not stop in the city of Balaquia (Vallaki) and continue west to a settlement in Brescia called Santa Barovia (Krezk), where there will be a strong church that will protect Ireena. With their destination set, the group executes their plan: Ireena, disguised, gives her silvered short sword to Renoir after he promises to take care of her. The group prepares to leave Barovia's mist and begin their journey through the domain's dangerous roads.

title: 04.5 - The Flight from Barovia
content: Here is the English translation of your text, without any additions or inventions: Session Summary: The Flight from Barovia PCs present: Feyre (played by Rocío). Note: Although the rest of the group (Pulgar, Ceres, Broseph, Ladril Gabriel, Hulio, Erdan) are mentioned, this was a solo session played by Feyre. NPCs present: Irena (burgomaster's daughter), Vistani, Strahd von Zarovich, Vallaki Guards. Locations: Barovia, Old Svalich Road, Lake Zarovich (mentioned), Castle Ravenloft (seen in the distance), Vallaki (mentioned as Balaqui/Balaquia). Main Developments and Loose Ends Feyre, transformed into a horse, successfully escorts Irena from the village of Barovia to the fortified town of Vallaki. During the journey, they manage to survive an ambush by wolves, an unnatural magical storm, and a direct encounter with the lord of the region himself, Strahd von Zarovich. Thanks to the intervention of a mysterious flock of crows and Irena's persuasion at the town gates, they manage to find safety, at least temporarily. Loose ends: Who or what was the amorphous figure with the plague doctor mask that awaited them in the black carriage near the turnoff to Castle Ravenloft? Who was the intelligent, mysterious crow that helped them in the cabin? Feyre suspects it might be a high-level allied druid. The Vistani on the road whom Feyre nearly runs over and who cursed them may hold a grudge in the future. Strahd now knows Irena has fled and is furious at not being invited to the cabin. The rest of the group (who are traveling on foot behind them) will surely run into him or suffer the consequences of this escape. Why exactly did the previous group take Feyre's sword (which turns out to be a silver rapier) from her using the excuse that it was a "symbol"? Session Joke Towards the end of the game, as the DM (Nemo) and Rocío were enthusiastically discussing how the rest of the group was going to suffer their encounter with Strahd in the official Wednesday game, Nemo suddenly realized there was another player connected to the Discord voice channel, secretly listening to the secret session. Nemo's genuine reaction ("Shit, the monkey is here, fucking spy!") and Rocío's suggestion to hide the game video so as not to spoil the surprise generated the best and funniest meta moment of the night. Scenes Scene 1: Galloping Away PCs present: Feyre. NPCs present: Irena (Determined, practical woman with a lot of personality. She hides her face with a scarf and helmet to avoid recognition. Not a fussy damsel. Archetype: The brave protectee / Damsel not in distress). Location(s): Village of Barovia, road to the south, and bridge over a clear river. Loot obtained: None (in fact, Feyre's silver rapier was taken from her before they left). Scene Summary: After her father's funeral, Irena prepares to leave Barovia. As Feyre's sword was taken under the guise of using it as a symbol for a costume, Irena must carry a weapon for defense. Feyre transforms into a riding horse, a saddle is placed on her, and Irena mounts her. They leave the village, crossing a bridge over a clear river, beginning their long journey along the winding Svalich Road. Scene 2: The Crossroads and the Vistani Curse PCs present: Feyre. NPCs present: Vistani (Five nomadic humans in gypsy-like attire, servants of the dark lord and the only ones capable of crossing the cursed fog. Archetype: Mysterious outsiders / Minions). Location(s): Intersection of the river with an old gallows and mist-shrouded graves. Loot obtained: None. Scene Summary: Upon reaching a crossroads marked by a gallows with a frayed rope, they decide to ignore the path towards Lake Zarovich (home of Madame Eva) and continue west towards Vallaki. Shortly after, they come head-on with a group of five Vistani pulling a mule and a cart. Feyre decides not to slow down and speeds past, nearly hitting one of them. The man moves aside at the last second, cursing them loudly while another makes a move to throw a stone that falls short. Scene 3: The Carriage of Red Eyes PCs present: Feyre. NPCs present: Strahd's Emissary (Amorphous figure, small, wrapped in a dark coat and wearing a long-nosed plague doctor mask. Archetype: The sinister herald). Location(s): Fallen gates marking the boundaries of Barovia and the turnoff to Castle Ravenloft. Loot obtained: None. Scene Summary: After an hour and a half of riding, they spot the imposing Castle Ravenloft looming on the mountain in the distance. Upon reaching the fork leading to the castle, they encounter a terrifying black carriage pulled by dark horses with red eyes that exhale mist from their muzzles. Atop the carriage awaits a masked creature that raises its hand, attempting to deliver a message, but Feyre, terrified, speeds past, ignoring it completely and crossing the ruined gates to exit the initial valley. Scene 4: The Climate of Terror and the Wolves PCs present: Feyre. NPCs present: Wild wolves (Forest beasts. Archetype: Predators / Servants of darkness). Location(s): Forests and hills on the old road. Loot obtained: None. Scene Summary: The daylight sky darkens unnaturally in a matter of minutes. A torrential downpour, accompanied by lightning and thunder, turns day into night. Irena, looking at the sky, recognizes in terror that this is the work of "Strahd." As they ride through the downpour, Feyre senses that a pack of wolves is ambushing them from the thicket. Reacting in time, Feyre accelerates and manages to outrun the beasts before they can reach their legs. Scene 5: The Gallows' Shelter and the Lord of Barovia PCs present: Feyre. NPCs present:  Strahd von Zarovich (Noble, regal, and pale figure. He wears no armor, a soaked cloak, and his eyes glow red. He controls the weather at will, and his presence radiates mystical terror. Archetype: The Dark Lord / Relentless Villain).*  Mysterious Crow (Bird with an intelligent gaze, capable of understanding speech and communicating. Archetype: The unexpected ally / Nature's guide).* Location(s): An elevated road and an abandoned stone and wood mountain shelter (containing the corpse of a hanged man). Loot obtained: None. Scene Summary: Strahd appears before them, leaping from a cliff onto the road. To Irena's terror, Feyre tries to turn back and flee, but Strahd throws magical projectiles that severely wound Feyre (still in horse form). They manage to take refuge in a dark mountain cabin, only to discover the corpse of a hanged man swaying from the rafters. Strahd arrives at the door and, in a polite but menacing tone, demands entry to reclaim "what is his." Feyre refuses to invite him in. At that moment, a very intelligent crow enters through a crack. Feyre (using Animal Handling) communicates with it. The bird flies outside and summons a vast horde of crows that attack Strahd. While the vampire defends himself from the birds (and giant bats that appear to assist him), Feyre transforms back into a horse and flees at full gallop with Irena. Scene 6: The Gates of Vallaki PCs present: Feyre. NPCs present: Irena. Vallaki Guards (Grim soldiers watching from atop a palisade. Archetype: The border guards). Location(s): Exterior and fortified gates of Vallaki (Balaqui). Loot obtained: None. Scene Summary: After ignoring a detour towards an old mill, they finally spot the town of Vallaki. It is a burgh surrounded by a 5-meter wooden palisade, with watchtowers, torches, and wolf heads impaled on pikes in front of the iron gates. They arrive exhausted and soaked, but the gates are closed for the night. The guards refuse to open, following regulations, but Irena reveals her identity as the daughter of the burgomaster of Barovia and uses all her persuasion (and subtle threats) to convince them. The guards finally yield, opening the heavy gates and allowing both to find refuge within the town walls.
snippet: Here is the English translation of your text, without any additions or inventions: Session Summary: The Flight from Barovia PCs present: Feyre (played by Rocío). Note: Although the rest of the group (Pulgar, Ceres, Broseph, Ladril Gabriel, Hulio, Erdan) are mentioned, this was a solo session played

title: 05 - Ravenloft's Crossroads
content: Session Summary: Ravenloft's Crossroads: Invitations and Bats PCs present: Broseph (Juan Maldonado), Ceres (Paloma), Pulgar (Juan Casanova), Ladril Gabriel (Álvaro), Erdan (Marcos), Feyre (Rocío - mentioned/in horse form). (Note: Hulio was not present). NPCs present: The Priest (Donavich), Ismark (also referred to as "Nacho"), Irena, Gypsies/Vistani, Madlock (driver), Strahd von Zarovich. Main events and loose ends: Main events: The group attends the funeral of the former burgomaster and discovers that the population seems to suffer from a soul sickness or chronic depression, and that the souls of dead adventurers march towards Ravenloft every night. They prepare a decoy: Irena and Feyre (transformed into a horse) leave on their own. The main group travels in a luxurious carriage, ignoring some gypsies on the road. At a crossroads, they receive an invitation to dinner from Strahd. The group splits: Broseph and Erdan accept and go to the castle, while Ceres, Pulgar, and Ladril continue. Strahd intercepts the latter's carriage, discovers Irena's deception, laughs at the situation, and unleashes a swarm of bats from which they barely manage to escape. Loose ends: What will happen to Broseph and Erdan now that they have entered Castle Ravenloft as guests? Where exactly are Irena and Feyre, and will they manage to reach their destination (Vallaki) safely? What were the gypsies really carrying under the canvas of their wagon? Will the curse/evil eye cast by the gypsies when they passed have any effect? Session Joke: "The Hitchhiker". When the dark lord of Barovia himself, Strahd von Zarovich, makes a dramatic entrance in the middle of a storm, leaping from a cliff to block the road and cast a spell, the tension was through the roof. However, Paloma (Ceres) decides to treat him as a mere traffic obstacle, attempting to swerve around him with the carriage. After braking sharply mere inches from him, they joke about calling the terrifying vampire a "hitchhiker," breaking the epic tension with a laugh from the Master himself. Honorable mention to Pulgar (Juan Casanova) "building a rectangular brick" in the bathroom while leafing through a book of demonology. Scene 1: The Funeral of Empty Souls PCs present: Broseph, Erdan, Ceres, Pulgar.    NPCs present: The Priest (deranged, jealous of his prominence, with dark circles under his eyes), Ismark, Irena (dressed in mourning), Villagers (lost gaze, apathetic, "walking dead" - archetype of hopeless victims*). Location: Barovia Village Cemetery. Loot obtained: None (Pulgar inspects the graves but deduces they are of poor adventurers). Summary: The funeral of the burgomaster takes place all morning. Broseph, Erdan, and Ceres notice that the villagers are not crying; they seem empty, victims of a kind of trauma or "soul sickness" generated by Barovia's environment. Ceres offers a bright prayer for the corpse, which provokes the jealousy of the local priest, who is deranged by having his son locked up. When questioned by Pulgar, the priest reveals that every night the ghosts of dead adventurers march in procession from the cemetery to Castle Ravenloft and never return, which terrifies Ceres regarding the fate of their own souls. Scene 2: Preparations and an Ungrateful Burgomaster PCs present: Broseph, Erdan, Ceres, Pulgar, Ladril Gabriel.    NPCs present: Ismark ("Nacho", defensive, offended - archetype of proud local noble*), Irena (disguised as an adventurer). Location: Burgomaster's House (Barovia Village).    Loot obtained: A silver rapier* (appropriated from Ismark under the guise of the disguise). A book on demonology and logic (read by Erdan). Summary: The group finalizes the plan to get Irena out of the village. They disguise her as an adventurer (referred to as "Nacho's" disguise) and have her ride Feyre, who has transformed into a horse, with them leaving first. While they wait, Broseph tries to talk to Ismark about the village's mental illness, but Ismark takes offense as the new burgomaster. The PCs (especially Ceres and Broseph) deem him ungrateful and proud, considering they are risking their lives for his sister. Pulgar calms things down to avoid a fight, but the group leaves with a bad taste in their mouths, stealing the family's silver rapier and taking their luxurious carriage and the remaining horses. Scene 3: The Gibbet and the Gypsy Wagon PCs present: Ceres (driving the carriage), Ladril, Broseph, Pulgar, Erdan.    NPCs present: Group of Gypsies/Vistani (with a woodcutter's axe, seemingly friendly but suspicious - archetype of hustlers/mysterious merchants*). Location: Roads outside Barovia, Ivlis River, Gibbet Crossroads. Loot obtained: None. Summary: The group departs in the luxurious carriage driven by Ceres. They reach a crossroads with a gibbet where Ceres has a hallucination and sees her own corpse hanging from the rope. Continuing on the road, they run head-on into a gypsy wagon. Although they try to stop them to talk or trade, Ceres refuses to stop due to haste. Pulgar closes the curtains assuming they want to rob them, and Ladril prepares to kick them if they approach. The gypsies are left with words in their mouths, throw a stone at them, and cast an evil eye upon the departing carriage. Scene 4: The Dark Lord's Invitation PCs present: Ceres, Ladril, Pulgar, Broseph, Erdan.    NPCs present: Madlock/Igor (Strahd's driver, gnome-sized, wears a plague mask and patched clothes - archetype of repulsive and loyal servant*). Location: Crossroads (Towards Vallaki and towards Ravenloft). Loot obtained: Invitation letter sealed by Strahd von Zarovich. Summary: The group encounters an imposing black carriage pulled by black horses. The doors open by themselves, and a strange servant named Madlock hands them a letter. It is a formal invitation from Strahd to dine at the castle, guaranteeing their safety on the journey. The group debates heatedly: Ladril, Ceres, and Pulgar refuse to go, prioritizing their mission to protect Irena. However, Broseph (driven by curiosity) and Erdan decide to accept the invitation to get answers. Both get out of the carriage and board the black carriage, thus dividing the group. Scene 5: Welcome to Ravenloft PCs present: Broseph, Erdan. NPCs present: Strahd von Zarovich (noble and distant figure, drinking a glass of blood). Location: Precipice and drawbridge of Castle Ravenloft. Loot obtained: None. Summary: The black carriage takes Broseph and Erdan through a rugged landscape to the terrifying Castle Ravenloft. Upon arriving at the torch-lit courtyard, Broseph's keen perception allows him to see Strahd on a very high balcony drinking blood wine. Broseph gives him a polite salute; in response, Strahd transforms into a bat and flies west, leaving the two mages at the castle gates. Scene 6: The Hitchhiker and the Swarm PCs present: Ceres, Ladril, Pulgar.    NPCs present: Strahd von Zarovich (noble, pale, red eyes, arrogant and amused attitude - archetype of untouchable villain*). Location: Muddy and rainy road in the forest. Loot obtained: None. Summary: As Ceres, Ladril, and Pulgar advance under a storm, lightning illuminates Strahd leaping from a cliff into the middle of the road. Ceres masterfully slams on the brakes just in front of him. Strahd approaches, pets the horse, and demands to see inside the carriage looking for Irena. Pulgar and Ladril try to lie to him, saying they were ambassadors, but Strahd pulls out a crystal ball and realizes the decoy. Far from being enraged, he finds the trick hilarious. He laughs heartily under the thunder, congratulates Ceres (knowing her friend is the horse), and raises his arms, summoning hundreds of bats. Strahd disappears, transformed within the swarm, which begins to attack ferociously. Ladril expends divine magic ("Intervention") and his own sword to protect the horses from bites; Pulgar locks himself in the carriage, securing all latches so that not a single bat can enter; and Ceres, with an incredible Animal Handling roll, manages to calm the horses' blind stampede, heal one of them, and guide the carriage at full speed to leave the cloud of bats behind.

title: 05 - Tutorial Combate Spacial
content: Here is the session summary based on the provided transcript. Scaling in Borite and Combat Maneuvers PCs present Captain Nemo (Leader and "face" of the group) Paloma (Pilot) Rocío (Gunner/Marine) Emilio (Communications and Sensors) Alvarito/Fomega (Engineer and Sensors) Juan/Jimmy Balder (Marine and support) NPCs present Blaine (Simulation instructor, likely an AI or unelaborated crew member)    Krusch (Mentioned - Pirate Captain of the Miseries Company*) Holmer (Mentioned - Merchant and contact)    Daniel Blau (Mentioned - Captain of the Sarcomond*) Important developments in the PCs' lives or for the campaign The crew confirms their next objective: locate the pirates in the Borite system before the trail goes cold. The long-term plan is established to abduct Doctora Torcan on the planet Talasa (Ipres sector) to obtain secrets about organic tissues. The players' ship has suffered critical damage to the jump drive (a -2 penalty) and hull due to a failed attempt to refuel in a gas giant, forcing them to spend funds on repairs and fuel. The crew becomes familiar with space combat protocols and their ship's capabilities, discovering they have considerable firepower but defensive shortcomings (lack of sandcasters). Loose ends    Investigation on the surface of Borite to find the trail of the Miseries Company*. The urgent need to repair the ship's hull hit points and jump drive. Acquire defensive countermeasures (sandcasters) and missiles for future real combat. Intelligence Review and Flight Plan PCs present: All. NPCs present: None (Mention of previous contacts). Location: Inside the ship, in transit to Borite. Ships: Miseries Company (Scout, Captain Krusch), Sarcomond (Captain Daniel Blau). The crew reviews information previously obtained through the merchant Holmer. They confirm that the Miseries Company, captained by Krusch, sold high-value "computer scrap" in Torpol before fleeing to Borite after an encounter with the ship Sarcomond. They also discuss the mission commissioned by an "aunt in orbit" (possibly Lady Hil or an associate) to abduct the geneticist Doctora Torcan on Talasa. Due to a previous incident piloting near a gas giant, the ship has a damaged jump drive and a weakened hull. Captain Nemo decides that upon arrival at Borite, they will buy unrefined fuel to process it on board, rather than risking collecting it again. Arrival at Borite and Logistics PCs present: All. NPCs present: None directly. Location: Spaceport or orbit of Borite (Borite System). Upon arriving in the system, work is divided. Paloma and Nemo handle ship matters: buying fuel and overseeing refining and basic repairs. Meanwhile, Juan (Jimmy) and Alvarito (Fomega) prepare to go ashore and investigate the pirates' trail, attempting to be discreet. The need to save money ("machacantes") is emphasized, as hull repairs are extremely costly. Combat Simulation: The Cowardly Hare PCs present: All. NPCs present: Blaine (Simulator Instructor). Location: Holodeck / Ship's simulator. Ships: Banshee (Harrier, PCs' Ship), Cowardly Hare (Free Trader / Freighter). Blaine sets up virtual scenarios to train the crew in space combat. In the first scenario, they face a merchant freighter attempting to flee. Roles: Paloma pilots, Nemo coordinates (Leadership), Rocío handles turrets, Emilio takes care of electronic warfare, and Fomega manages sensors/engineering. Action: Emilio manages to block the enemy's communications to prevent them from calling for help. The ship proves to be far superior in speed and armament. Rocío fires the particle battery, causing massive damage that incapacitates the freighter, forcing its surrender. They learn the importance of managing thrust and distances. Combat Simulation: The Wolf in Sheep's Clothing PCs present: All. NPCs present: Blaine (Instructor). Location: Holodeck / Ship's simulator. Ships: Banshee (Harrier, PCs' Ship), Q-Ship (Armed trap freighter). The second scenario presents a ship that appears to be a vulnerable merchant but turns out to be a trap (Q-Ship) with hidden turrets. Development: The combat is much tougher. The PCs' ship suffers simulated critical damage, including the destruction of the jump drive. Tactics: The use of missiles is tested. They discover that although they are expensive and can be intercepted, if they hit, they cause devastating damage (multiplied by the attack's effect). Conclusion: Although they win the simulation, the crew realizes how vulnerable they are to critical hull damage and the imperative need to acquire defenses against missiles and lasers. Captain Nemo ends the training session.

title: 05.5 - The Dinner
content: Here is the English translation of the provided text, without adding or inventing anything: Session: Dinner with the Devil at Castle Ravenloft PCs present: Erdan (played by Marcos), Broseph (played by Juan Maldonado), Renoir (played by Nacho). (Paloma was present on the call, but her character did not actively participate in the scenes). NPCs present: Rahadin, Vistani Servants, Strahd von Zarovich. Mentions of Madame Eva, Tatiana, and Ireena. Major developments and loose ends Major developments: The group arrives at Castle Ravenloft and is received with terrifying hospitality. Strahd von Zarovich confirms that the adventurers' souls have belonged to him from the moment they entered Barovia and that they are trapped in his domain for eternity for his entertainment. Strahd grants them permission to wander the castle as his "guests," but immediately lowers a portcullis, leaving them locked inside.    Out of character:* The characters level up to Level 4 for having fulfilled the milestone of bringing Ireena safely to Vallaki. Loose ends: How will they escape Castle Ravenloft now that the exit portcullis is closed? What kind of traps and "ancient creatures" did Strahd mention inhabit the castle? What is the exact meaning of the procession of souls marching towards the castle at night, and how will it affect Erdan, who is obsessed with studying them? Will they be able to visit Madame Eva if they manage to escape alive, as they promised the Vistani and Strahd? Session Joke Session Joke: During the tense dinner, Strahd notices that Renoir smells of Ireena's perfume and asks if he has tried to deceive him by disguising himself as her. Renoir (Nacho), instead of being scared, proudly admits that using women's costumes and imitating Ireena's voice is one of his fun tricks. The table erupts in laughter (and astonishment) when the Dungeon Master describes Strahd being quite pleased with this response, even looking at him with "desire," creating the ironic and comical situation where the bard has accidentally seduced the vampire dark lord by dressing as his beloved. Scene 1: Arrival Under the Storm and the Herald of Souls PCs present: Erdan, Broseph, Renoir. NPCs present:    Mysterious Coachman (Silent, doesn't even turn his head to say goodbye; Archetype: Automaton Servant*).    Rahadin (Elf, dark skin, long hair, wears a grey cloak over black studded leather armor and an elegant scimitar at his belt. He is surrounded by an invisible choir of thousands of tormented souls accusing him of having killed them; Archetype: Sinister Servant / Herald of Death*). Place(s): Outer Courtyard, Dragon Vestibule, and Great Hall of Castle Ravenloft. Loot obtained: None. Summary of the scene: The carriage leaves the adventurers in the enormous, misty courtyard of Castle Ravenloft under an increasing rain. The coachman abandons them without a word. Upon entering, they pass through double doors into a vaulted vestibule guarded by four red dragon whelp statues that seem to watch them. They then proceed to a dusty great hall with eight gargoyles on the ceiling. Rahadin, the elven chamberlain, descends the grand staircase. His very presence emits an aura of tormented souls so strong that Renoir takes psychic damage (mitigated by the DM) and becomes terrified. Rahadin, with a forced and chilling smile, welcomes them and guides them to a waiting room before retiring. Scene 2: The Waiting Room and the Vistani's Bets PCs present: Erdan, Broseph, Renoir. NPCs present:    Vistani Servants (Three women and one man, prepare the banquet while laughing and betting on the adventurers' imminent death; Archetype: Indifferent Minions*). Place(s): Guest Waiting Room (with ornamental armor and spiral staircase) and doors to the Main Dining Room. Loot obtained: Appetizers (nuts, almonds, raisins, wine). (Note: Renoir loses a silver coin by gifting it to a servant). Summary of the scene: While waiting in a room with appetizers, Erdan stealthily peeks through the half-open doors of the grand dining room and discovers Vistani servants preparing a lavish banquet while laughing and betting that the adventurers will not leave the castle alive. Renoir bursts into the room noisily, greets the servants, tells them of his intention to visit Madame Eva, and, winking to show he has heard them, gives a silver coin to a servant saying, "I bet we get out." Broseph enters to politely ask for his nut bowl to be refilled. The servants kindly usher them out of the room and leave the castle through the main door. The adventurers wait for a while, investigating the spiral staircase, until a musical din startles them. Scene 3: Banquet with the God of Barovia PCs present: Erdan, Broseph, Renoir. NPCs present:    Strahd von Zarovich (Vampire, wears elegant and dry clothes, although his hair and ring are damp from the rain. Drinks blood from a goblet. Expressive, jaded, cold, arrogant attitude with flashes of absolute evil when imposing his dominion; Archetype: Dark Lord / Self-Proclaimed God*). Place(s): Main Dining Room of Castle Ravenloft (decorated with mirrors, chandeliers, a large table laden with exquisite delicacies, and an imposing pipe organ adorned with statues of writhing souls). Loot obtained: None (manjares and dinner viands are consumed). Summary of the scene: The doors swing open to the sound of an intense melody played on a massive pipe organ. The characters enter and discover Strahd von Zarovich playing masterfully. After an attempt by Renoir to accompany him on the violin, Strahd rises, welcomes them to Barovia, and declares himself lord of all they see. He crudely explains that their souls belong to him and that he has brought them simply to alleviate his eternal boredom. He asks them to entertain him: Broseph introduces himself as an investigative sorcerer, Erdan reluctantly shows him his necromancy spellbook (which Strahd despises as if it were a "notebook for school children"), and Renoir skillfully plays the ocarina. Strahd speaks to them of the echo of gods and asserts that he is the only God in those lands, showing absolute emptiness when speaking of his lost love, Tatiana. After being pleased by Renoir's music (and his confession about cross-dressing as Ireena), Strahd grants them his hospitality, allowing them to wander the castle under the warning not to disturb the "ancient creatures." He majestically withdraws, and, just as he leaves, the group hears the unmistakable sound of a heavy metal portcullis closing, trapping them inside.
