title: 62 - PoD - Reagrupandose
content: Here is the session summary following the requested pattern and in Spanish from Spain. Clear Accounts and Broken Ships PCs present: Honor Boone, Daijiro, Pika, (Nemo's and Nacho's PCs). NPCs present: Krrsh, Princess Rao (Pragmatic and direct), Prince Harrick (Tired but proud), Lady Hil (Diplomatic), Chief Galx (Mentioned as a contact). Campaign Development:    Financial Reorganization: The Ginger*'s accounts have been settled following the sale of merchandise (Common Electronics) and advanced weapons. Debts with the deceased Goran Dragic have been paid off, and Daijiro has been integrated into the Letters of Marque and the crew as his practical replacement. Krrsh's Operations: The Vargr privateer has been patrolling the trade route (Sindalia Main). He has had encounters with imperial freighters and Aslan, achieving considerable loot (almost 3 million credits), although his ship suffered severe damage in the process. Drinax Logistics: After the battle, Drinax is full of foreigners (crews from Birni, Clarke, representatives from Blue). This complicates discretion and resupply, as there are not enough shipyards or spare parts for everyone. Route Planning: A new short-term action plan has been drawn up: travel to Hilfer for repairs and purchases, jump to Ergo to investigate a stranded ship (possible component salvage), and finally go to Kteiroa to fulfill the deal with Utea. Loose Ends: The Salvage at Ergo: It is known that there is a "dead" ship on the planet Ergo (red zone), which could contain the power plant Utea needs. Environmental (radiation) and hostile dangers of the planet remain to be ascertained. Diplomacy with Birni: It is still pending to see how the invitation of the regent of Birni to King Oleb evolves. Lady Hil suggests that any information about the ancient Sindal Empire (possibly an expert on Dostoevsky) would be helpful. Utea's Commission: The industrial components (power plant, water recycling, pipes) to be delivered in Kteiroa in exchange for the spy network are still missing. Session Joke: During recruitment on the surface of Drinax (among the Vespexers), Nemo's PC, who considers himself a local hero ("people know me"), rolls an absolute critical failure (double 1) on his Social roll. The table erupts in laughter, joking that instead of being received as a hero, people want to lynch him or that his fame is terrible. The GM (Juan) resolves it narratively by saying that, due to the presence of foreigners, he must be extremely discreet so as not to reveal that he is a pirate, turning the failure into a moment of comedic tension. Settling Accounts and Krrsh's Loot PCs present: Honor Boone, Daijiro, Pika, (Nemo's and Nacho's PCs). NPCs present: Krrsh (Vargr, aggressive and reckless, mentioned through mechanics). Location: Drinax (Drinax/Sindal). Ships: Ginger (Harrier, Captain Honor Boone), Scout (Scout Model, Captain Krrsh). Summary: The session begins with Honor Boone and the group crunching numbers. The profits from sales in Cordan are clarified, and the estate of the deceased Goran Dragic is managed. Immediately after, Krrsh's activity and his ship Scout are resolved through an abstract mini-game. The players roll for him: Krrsh attacks imperial and Aslan freighters, sometimes unarmed and other times with nasty surprises. He achieves a "jackpot" (3 million credits) but his ship ends up in the red, with severe structural damage after engaging escorted ships. The tithe for King Oleb XVI is calculated. War Damages and Logistics PCs present: Honor Boone, Daijiro, Pika. Location: Floating Palace (Drinax/Sindal). Ships: Maui (Mercenary Cruiser, Captain Nemo/Nacho), Ginger (Harrier, Captain Honor Boone). Summary: The condition of the Maui and the Ginger after the Battle of Drinax is assessed. The Maui has hull and critical damages, and the Ginger needs maintenance. Upon attempting repairs in Drinax, they discover that the system is saturated and lacks industrial resources. They decide to use their own spare parts to patch up essentials (spending tons of cargo on field repairs). The need to leave the system to find competent shipyards and supplies becomes evident. Audiences at the Floating Palace PCs present: Honor Boone, Pika, Daijiro, (Nacho's PC). NPCs present: Princess Rao (Pragmatic, Noble administrator), Prince Harrick (Melancholy but satisfied, Tired warrior), Lady Hil (Astute, Diplomat). Location: Royal Court, Floating Palace (Drinax/Sindal). Summary: The group meets with royalty. Honor Boone informs Princess Rao about the mission in Cordan and Goran's death; Rao accepts Daijiro into the Letters of Marque under the captain's criteria. Prince Harrick offers his condolences for Goran and praises the performance of Blue's prototype fighters, suggesting promoting that industry. Pika speaks with Lady Hil about the delicate diplomatic situation with Birni and the possible visit of King Oleb; Hil emphasizes the importance of obtaining experts in Sindal history to impress the Birnians. It is made clear that Drinax does not want pirates to "defecate where they eat": they must sell their hauls on other worlds to gain influence, not on Drinax. Recruitment and Roadmap PCs present: Honor Boone, Daijiro, (Nemo's PC, Nacho's PC). Location: Vespexer Settlements (Drinax/Sindal). Summary: The group defines their plan: go to Hilfer (where there is technology) to repair the ships and buy the machinery for Utea, then stop by Ergo to salvage an abandoned ship that Daijiro has news of, and finally go to Kteiroa. They need extra crew (gunners and pilots). Nemo's and Nacho's PCs go down to the surface to recruit among the Vespexers and ex-convicts. Despite a dice fumble, they manage to get basic crew (cannon fodder and operators), although they don't find specialists like astrogators. They prepare to leave Drinax for Hilfer.

title: 63 -PoD - De compras
content: Session Title: Logistics, Purchases, and the Divided Fleet PCs Present: Lyra, Fenix, Clayton, Daijiro, Yaang-ki, Pika NPCs Present: Krrsh, Polona, Zerachiel, Giaquintos, Goizader, Jimmy (mentioned), King Oleb XVI (mentioned). Main Campaign Development: The characters dedicate the session to reorganizing their resources after acquiring a second ship (The Maui). The group consolidates into a small fleet, dividing the crew between The Ginger and The Maui. A significant investment of community and personal funds is made to re-equip the characters with better armor (Cloth TL12), specialized weaponry (twin laser pistols), and to hire new crew to cover vacant positions. The strategy is decided to keep The Ginger as the "fearsome pirate" ship (leveraging Oleb's ship's reputation) and The Maui as a cargo/diplomatic vessel. The next established route is Drinax -> Hilfer -> Ergo. Loose Ends: False Identities: Lyra wants to obtain false documentation, but the GM indicates this requires roleplaying or a "mini-adventure" and not simply buying it. It remains pending to define what exact identities they want (Blue? Borite?). Fenix's Career Benefit: Nemo (Fenix) mentions a benefit from his spy career (secret identity/science equipment) that he did not note at the time. It remains pending to review his notes or speak with the GM to define it. Loot Distribution: Although a common fund is decided for now, the discussion about how future profits will be distributed (pirate parts system: Captain x5, Officers x2, Crew x1) now that there are two captains remains latent. Session Gag: During the purchase of the custom twin laser pistols for Daijiro and Yaang-ki, the GM describes that when put together they form an image. They offer options: the wings of Sindal's dragon, a face split in two, or... a foreskin. Juan (Daijiro) categorically rejects the foreskin option ("No, not foreskin"), provoking laughter at the absurd offer of Sindalite "art." Scene 1: Fleet Organization and Finances PCs Present: Lyra, Fenix, Clayton, Daijiro, Yaang-ki, Pika Locations: Spaceport (Drinax) Ships: The Ginger (Far Trader, Captain Lyra), The Maui (Far Trader, Captain Fenix) Summary: The group gathers in Drinax after their latest adventures. It is clarified that there were no major events in the previous session (where players were absent), except for the acquisition of the fief. Economic management is intensely discussed: although The Maui technically belongs to Pika (after Goran's death), Fenix will act as captain. The future loot distribution is debated, establishing that for now a common fund will be used for repairs and equipment before distributing personal profits. The hierarchy is established, and it is confirmed they will go with both ships towards Hilfer and then to Ergo. Scene 2: Shopping in the Drinax Market PCs Present: Lyra, Fenix, Clayton, Daijiro, Yaang-ki, Pika Locations: Market / Spaceport (Drinax) Summary: Paloma (Lyra) coordinates a communal and personal shopping list. Weaponry: Daijiro and Yaang-ki order a pair of twin laser pistols (which form a drawing when put together) for 15,000 credits. Fenix buys armor-piercing ammunition for his rifle and laser sights. Protection: Cloth (Synth-silk) armor of TL12 is purchased for almost all PCs and one extra for Krrsh. These are high-tech, lightweight armors that can be worn under clothing or vacuum suits.    Technology and Miscellaneous: Bugs* (TL11 spy microphones/cameras), long-range radio transceivers (for ship-to-ship communication on the surface), expert software (Astrogation, Combat), and a laser ring for Yaang-ki are acquired.    Medical: Medikits, trauma packs*, and anti-radiation drugs are restocked. Scene 3: Crew Recruitment and Assignment PCs Present: Lyra, Fenix, Clayton, Daijiro, Yaang-ki, Pika NPCs Present: Polona (Pilot, Young novice), Zerachiel (Engineer), Giaquintos (Marine/Muscle), Goizader (Gunner, 18 years old). Locations: Spaceport (Drinax) Summary: Having two ships, the group needs to cover vacant positions. They decide to hire four new crew members (generic NPCs for now, possibly novices from Drinax).    For The Ginger*: A Gunner (Goizader) and an Engineer (Zerachiel) are assigned.    For The Maui*: A Pilot (Polona) and a Marine/Muscle (Giaquintos) are assigned. The PCs are distributed between the ships (Pika, Fenix, and Yaang-ki on one; Lyra, Clayton, and Daijiro on the other, although the exact distribution varied during the conversation). The new crew members are equipped with ballistic vests and basic weapons from the ship's arsenal. Scene 4: The Fleet's Image PCs Present: Lyra, Fenix, Clayton, Daijiro, Yaang-ki, Pika Locations: Interior of the ships (Drinax) Summary: Lyra raises the question of whether they should conceal or paint The Ginger's hull to cover the "redhead" image and avoid being recognized as pirates. Fenix and the group debate the utility of intimidation. They conclude that it is beneficial for The Ginger to maintain its appearance to earn a reputation as "Fearsome Pirates" (making it easier for targets to surrender without a fight), while The Maui will maintain a lower profile as a cargo or diplomatic vessel. They prepare to jump to the Hilfer system in the next session.

title: 64 - Hilfer eng
content: Session Summary: Hilfer Layover and Echoes of the Past PCs present: Nemo, Fénix, Yaang-ki, Daijiro, Lyra, (and the character played by Álvaro). NPCs present: Nicolás Alexander (and his belter family), Oleri, Link. (Mentioned during the session: King Oleb XVI, Krrsh, Jimmy, Scholar Voha, Thao Poloc, Ferrik Redthane, Miria Silverhand, Pika, Polona, Zerakiel, Goizender). Main Developments and Campaign Goal (Kingdom of Drinax) End of the Siege: After months of extreme tension, the Ihatei siege on Drinax has ended. The kingdom remains standing thanks to the recent alliances forged by the PCs with the Clarke, Blue, and Byrni systems. Kingdom Expansion: King Oleb XVI is expected to attend the Byrni system to formally finalize the union with Drinax, which would place a vital border beacon for the ambitions of restoring the Kingdom. Additionally, the PCs have been named Marquesses of Inús. Search for Funding: The Drinax coffers are emptying. The crew is heading to the restricted planet of Ergo in search of the treasure of a crashed ancient smuggler ship (based on a lead from Jimmy Largo) to obtain funds and equipment. Loose Ends The privateer Krrsh is successfully pirating throughout the Dustbelt (Indalian Main), but Jimmy's whereabouts are unknown following his mission to Thalassa. Scholar Voha remains trapped on Dostoevsky, waiting to travel to Drinax.    The crew stole the Martin III*, an Imperial treasure ship, which is currently hidden and being modified in Drinax. The secret risks being leaked soon.    The pirate Miria Silverhand (captain of the Mercy Fudge*) is operating with impunity in the Hilfer system, stealing ships from local miners. What secret information about Ergo did the local at the bar have, for which he asked for 500 credits? Why did a recent registry show a massive food shipment destined for the radioactive and forbidden world of Ergo, before being "corrected" to Falcon? Session Joke Álvaro's character, trying to act tough and wealthy in a pilot's bar to get information on routes to Ergo, gets a contact to ask him for a 500-credit bribe. When he goes to pay, Álvaro checks his inventory live and realizes he is absolutely broke, pathetically offering some "Blue little cigars" as the only currency, to the laughter of the rest of the table. Session Scenes Scene 1: The Weight of the Crown and the Jump to Hilfer PCs present: Nemo, Fénix, Yaang-ki, Daijiro, Lyra NPCs present: None (GM Recap) Location(s): Deep Space / Hyperspace (Drinax - Hilfer Route) Ships: Maui (Aslan Freighter, Captain Fénix), Ginger (Raider Freighter) Summary:  While traveling through hyperspace, the crew reflects on the agonizing months spent defending Drinax from the Ihatei and the new political alliances (such as the one with Byrni). To solve their financial problems, they decide to go to Ergo to loot a crashed smuggler ship. They agree on an approach strategy: the Ginger (commanded by Pika and part of the NPC crew) will remain hidden in the system with sensors in passive mode to avoid drawing attention, while they will use the Maui (piloted by Polona) as the main ship to show their faces, dock at the Hilfer spaceport, seek information, and buy supplies for the radioactive exploration. Scene 2: SOS in the Void PCs present: Lyra, Nemo, Yaang-ki, Daijiro NPCs present: Nicolás Alexander (Father, belter miner, desperate and relieved; Archetype: Innocent civilian in distress) Location(s): Asteroid (Hilfer System) Ships: Maui (Aslan Freighter, Captain Fénix), Mercy Fudge (Pirate ship - Mentioned) Summary:  Upon exiting hyperspace in the Hilfer system, the Maui's sensors pick up a distress beacon. Deviating from their route, they land on an asteroid where they rescue Nicolás Alexander, his wife, and his three children. They had been rationing oxygen in their vacuum suits for hours after the infamous pirate Miria Silverhand (a former temporary ally of the crew on Theev) stole their home ship to put it in the Mercy Fudge's cargo hold. The belters, immensely grateful, are accommodated on the Maui. Although they don't know much about Ergo or distant systems, they provide some context about the harsh life in the Hilfer system. Scene 3: Dry Land and Skewers of Dubious Origin PCs present: Lyra, Nemo, Yaang-ki, Daijiro NPCs present: Various local merchants. Location(s): Spaceport and Downport (Hilfer) Ships: Maui (Aslan Freighter, Captain Fénix) Summary:  The Maui docks at the class B spaceport on Hilfer. After disembarking the Alexander family, the crew prepares to head down to the Downport. Informed of the strict Imperial laws of the spaceport and the planet, they leave their long arms and heavy armor on the ship, going down only with cloths (vests) and small knives. Upon stepping onto the surface, Hilfer's desert and extremely dry environment hits them. Yaang-ki, guided by hunger, ignores the aridity and approaches a street stall to devour some heavily spiced meat skewers, cooked over animal dung embers, washing them down with local cactus juice. Meanwhile, the group agrees to split efforts to search for spare parts (such as a water recycling plant) and gather intelligence on Ergo. Scene 4: Alleys, Failed Bribes, and Old Acquaintances PCs present: Lyra, Nemo, Daijiro, and Álvaro's character. NPCs present: Oleri (Ex-Imperial marine, crippled with an unreplaced stump, drunk; Archetype: Disgraced veteran), Link (Ex-Imperial marine, drunk; Archetype: Cantina gambler) Location(s): Taverns and Downport archives (Hilfer) Ships: Martin II / Martin III (Imperial treasure ship - Mentioned), Falcon (Ship or Destination - Mentioned) Summary:  The group splits up (with some PCs acting as security "shadows") to investigate without raising Imperial suspicion. Álvaro's character enters pilot cantinas looking for information on how to bypass Ergo, running into an informant who asks for 500 credits (money he doesn't have). Nemo, using a cover as a retired Vespexer scholar, infiltrates local databases looking for records on Ergo's radioactivity. Although everyone agrees that the surface is totally forbidden and monitored by Imperial satellites, Nemo finds a recent anomaly: a massive food cargo manifest that had Ergo as its original destination, subsequently corrected to Falcon. For her part, Lyra, pretending to be a corporate explorer, enters a local tavern and recognizes Oleri and Link playing cards; they are two veterans of the Imperial Navy and survivors of the Martin III, the same treasure ship that the former Drinax crew stole months ago.

NPCs present: Nicolás Alexander (and his belter family), Oleri, Link. (Mentioned during the session: King Oleb XVI, Krrsh, Jimmy, Scholar Voha, Thao Poloc,

title: 65 - Hilfer 2
content: Here is the summary of the session structured according to your instructions and translated into English: Thirst on Hilfer and the Trail of Ergo PCs present: Den, Pika, Klaiton, Lyra, Yaang-kee, Daijiro. NPCs present: O'Leary, Ealing, Informant pilot, Local beggars, Registry bureaucrat, Local gunners. Main character and campaign developments: The group discovers that the Kingdom of Drinax's reputation on Hilfer is abysmal due to past bombardments that destroyed the planet's water infrastructure. Upon learning that a local pirate, Miria Silverhand, is raiding ice harvesters and causing a humanitarian crisis due to lack of water, the group decides to intervene. Their goal is twofold: hunt the pirate to seize her ship (a 400-ton vessel equipped with a crane, ideal for their future expedition) and return the stolen water to the planet, presenting themselves as envoys of Drinax to clear the Kingdom's name. Loose ends:    Why did the freighter Garland* bring a massive shipment of food from a red, radioactive world like Ergo 13 years ago? What cargo and which passenger did an engineer take from Tech-World to the gas giant of Ergo in a local system ship?    The relentless Captain Jagad of the Third Imperium, now in command of the Comino, is following the trail of the characters' former corsair ship (Drinax Eagle / Banshee*) and has headed toward Goertel. The Session Joke: "The Hacker without his ChatGPT." During a Computers roll to access the spaceport archives, Klaiton tried to help Yaang-kee. However, they realized that Klaiton had lost his high-tech intrusion software (level 12) in the old mission against the Ihatei. Having become accustomed to the program doing everything for him "as if it were ChatGPT," Klaiton’s help was a disaster and actively "un-helped" the group, nearly triggering the government system's alarms if not for a correction to the roll. Scene 1: Card game with the ghosts of the Martin II PCs present: Pika. NPCs present: O'Leary (Right side of his face paralyzed, holds his inert arm, wears crew clothing without insignias. Archetype: Traumatized survivor), Ealing (Drunk as a skunk. Archetype: Retired spacer/Drinker). Location: Adobe bar (Hilfer).    Spaceships mentioned: Martin II (Freighter, Captain Torsa), Comino* (Pirate hunter, Captain Jagad).    Summary: Using a cover as a Clarke corporate prospector, Pika infiltrates a dice and card game in an adobe bar to gather information. There she meets O'Leary and Ealing, survivors of the Martin II*. O'Leary tells her how the pirates massacred part of the crew and abandoned them frozen in the desert, causing him permanent physical consequences. They warn Pika about the dangers of the frontier and reveal that Captain Jagad was on the planet a few months ago investigating the attack; Jagad now obsessively patrols the sector looking for a museum-looking ship, heading toward Goertel. Scene 2: Bureaucracy and hidden archives PCs present: Lyra, Yaang-kee, Klaiton, Den. NPCs present: None notable. Location: Spaceport administration offices (Hilfer).    Spaceships mentioned: Garland* (Freighter).    Summary: Den uses his silver tongue to legally access certain spaceport records, while Yaang-kee attempts to hack the rest of the customs system (with the clumsy "help" of Klaiton, who missed his old software). They discover that the ship involved in the Ergo manifests from 13 years ago is named Garland. Curiously, the ship used to import food from Asim, but it ceased its trade routes exactly on the date Drinax conquered Asim. Its first subsequent trip was the one that brought food from Ergo (later corrected to Falcon). The Garland* has been missing for years. Meanwhile, Lyra orders a water recycling plant for 80,000 credits. Scene 3: A secret trip to nowhere PCs present: Den, Klaiton, Daijiro. NPCs present: Informant pilot (Archetype: Smuggler/Opportunist). Location: Alleyways near the Spaceport (Hilfer). Spaceships mentioned: None specific. Summary: The group meets with the pilot contacted days ago and pays him the demanded 500 credits. The informant tells them a rumor he heard on Tech-World: a pilot was secretly hired by an engineer to take him and some mysterious crates to the gas giant of Ergo. Upon arrival, a system ship (without a jump drive) emerged from nowhere, picked up the passenger and the cargo, and disappeared, confirming there is a hidden base or facility in the system, bypassing the Third Imperium blockade. Scene 4: The drought and Silverhand's trail PCs present: Klaiton, Pika, Lyra, Yaang-kee, Daijiro, Den. NPCs present: Nicolás Alexander (Mentioned), Local beggars (Cracked and bleeding lips, malnourished, desperate. Archetype: Collateral civilian victims). Location: Streets and market (Hilfer).    Spaceships mentioned: MercyFuge* (400-ton corsair ship, Captain Miria Silverhand).    Summary: Daijiro follows the informant pilot, but the group's attention shifts when Klaiton interacts with some local Bedouins begging for a credit to buy water. They discover that Hilfer is suffering from a brutal shortage; Miria Silverhand and her heavily armed ship, the MercyFuge*, are terrorizing the "Belter" families who extract ice. Seeing a golden opportunity, the group (with Yaang-kee, Lyra, and Pika scouting the streets and radio communications) collects a pattern of attacks. Pika performs some brilliant astrogation calculations, narrowing down the pirate's hunting zone in the gas giant's asteroid belts. They draw up a plan: hunt the hunter. Scene 5: Stained contracts and hired gunners PCs present: Den, Daijiro. NPCs present: Two mercenary gunners (Locals seeking fortune. Archetype: Soldiers of fortune), Bureaucrat (Corruptible official). Location: Mercenary registry office (Hilfer).    Spaceships mentioned: Maui (Escort fighter, Polona [Pilot]), Ginger* (Armed freighter, Goizéder [Gunner]).    Summary: Preparing for space combat, the crew realizes they do not have enough competent gunners to crew the laser and missile weapons of the Maui and the Ginger*. Den and Daijiro head to the spaceport bars and recruit two local mercenaries by offering them 1,000 credits a week and a share of the loot. To avoid the Drinax corsairs' identities being legally registered, Den uses his false documentation. When the bureaucrat on duty notices the eye color on the passport doesn't match, Den subtly slides a 1,000-credit bribe, sealing the contract without further questions and preparing the fleet for the ambush.
snippet: Here is the summary of the session structured according to your instructions and translated into English: Thirst on Hilfer and the Trail of Ergo PCs present: Den, Pika, Klaiton, Lyra, Yaang-kee, Daijiro. NPCs present: O'Leary, Ealing, Informant pilot, Local beggars, Registry bureaucrat, Local gunner

title: 66 - Medalla de Plata
content: Here is the translation of the text into English: Here is the session summary structured according to your instructions, written in Peninsular Spanish (which has been translated to English) and using only the information provided in the transcript. Session Summary: Hilfer’s Bait and the Hunt for Miria PCs present: Lyra, Pika, Den, Klaiton, Yaang-ki, Daijiro. NPCs present/mentioned: Nicolás Alexander, Miria Silverhand, King Oleb XVI, Krrsh, Ferrik Redthane, Rufinus Aylil. Main campaign developments:  The crew has decided to act as benefactors and unofficial representatives of King Oleb XVI to win the loyalty and favor of the belters of the Hilfer system. By planning to end the threat posed by the pirate Miria Silverhand, they seek not only to improve the reputation of the Kingdom of Drinax and stabilize the local water economy, but also to seize the Mercy Future, a valuable ship owned by the Third Imperium. Loose ends: The imminent combat or negotiation with Miria Silverhand in the space junkyard. The rescue of the crew members left behind on the asteroid as bait. The pending expedition to the Ergo system to search for a lost ship.    Rumors regarding the whereabouts of the ship Águila del Sol (similar to the Banshee*), which remains lost in space. Session joke: The most fun moment at a meta-game level occurred when the game had to be briefly paused due to the crying of the GM's (Juan) young daughter. He explained that her pacifier had just been taken away and that the girl had a "broken heart." The table joked that this was nothing compared to the heartache she would give him when she started getting a boyfriend (or girlfriend). In addition, Nemo’s grand entrance arriving late and justifying it by saying "that lady ate tongue" generated quite a few laughs before they got tactical with the missiles. Scene 1: Logistics, Loot, and Repairs PCs present: Lyra, Pika, Den. NPCs present: None (Krrsh mentioned). Location(s): Shipyard / Spaceport (Hilfer). Ships mentioned:  Maui (300t Freighter, Captain Den) Ginger (Unknown, Captain Lyra) Harrier (Unknown, Unknown Captain - Mentioned) Scene summary: The crew spends some time at the shipyard reorganizing their finances and resources. They debate how to distribute the pirate loot so as not to repeat the resentment that occurred on the Harrier, deciding to simplify the model: Lyra will take 3 shares and the rest 1 share, while maintaining a common fleet fund (fed by Krrsh’s admiralty tithe) for general expenses. Subsequently, they buy tons of spare parts and manage to fully repair the critical hull damage of the Maui. They also discuss the purchase of medical supplies (trauma packs, panaceas, anti-rad) and browse manuals to buy an industrial surface vehicle (Hercules-class). Finally, they decide to scrap the idea of signing legal contracts before a notary with the gunners, preferring recruitment more typical of smugglers. Scene 2: Rumors in the Underworld PCs present: Lyra, Pika, Yaang-ki, Daijiro. NPCs present: Rufinus Aylil (Hustler/Local Informant, observer. Archetype: Underworld contact). Location(s): Underworld and Surface (Hilfer). Ships mentioned: None. Scene summary: Looking for information on Miria Silverhand’s base of operations, Lyra disguises herself and enters the Hilfer underworld accompanied by Yaang-ki and Daijiro (who monitor the reactions of the environment). After four days of investigation, they discover that Miria has no allies on the planet, as her actions are harming everyone. Taking advantage of the visit, Lyra bribes a local named Rufinus Aylil, who has family at the docks, with 300 credits so he can inform her in the future about cargo shipments and ship movements at the spaceport. Meanwhile, Pika tries to track Miria’s communications from the ship, but civilian sensors and excessive radio noise from the planet cause the roll to fail, confirming that the pirate is maintaining radio silence. Scene 3: Pact with the Belters PCs present: Lyra, Pika, Klaiton. NPCs present: Nicolás Alexander (Belter leader/contact. Archetype: Community spokesperson), King Oleb XVI (Mentioned). Location(s): Encrypted communications forum (Hilfer). Ships mentioned: None. Scene summary: Lyra contacts Nicolás Alexander and, through him, accesses a secure forum where the belter families communicate. With an epic speech, Lyra introduces herself as a representative of King Oleb XVI of Drinax, offering to take responsibility and help the oppressed community by eliminating Miria Silverhand. The belters accept happily, offering a reward of 50,000 credits. Pika and Lyra manage to persuade one of the wealthiest families to lend them a 20-ton shuttle to serve as bait for the trap. Scene 4: The Bait and the Hunt PCs present: Lyra, Pika, Den, Yaang-ki. NPCs present: Miria Silverhand (Aggressive pirate, confident. Archetype: Antagonist/Pirate). Location(s): Asteroid belt and deep space (Hilfer). Ships mentioned:  Belter Shuttle (20t Launch, Unknown Captain) Mercy Future (Salvage Hauler / 400t Imperial, Captain Miria Silverhand) Scene summary: Pika spends a day of work hacking the belter shuttle’s old operating system to install a hidden tracker (bug). They execute the plan: Den (disguised as a belter) and Yaang-ki fly the shuttle into the pirate’s hunting ground. Miria Silverhand takes the bait; she appears with the mammoth Mercy Future, fires a warning shot, and orders them to abandon the ship. Den and Yaang-ki are left stranded on an asteroid while Miria grabs the shuttle with her ship’s claw and carries it away. Thanks to Pika’s expertise, Miria does not detect the tracker in her communications. Scene 5: The Junkyard Hideout PCs present: Lyra, Pika, Den, Klaiton. NPCs present: Miria Silverhand (Mentioned). Location(s): Dark side of a moon (Hilfer). Ships mentioned:  Mercy Future (Salvage Hauler / 400t Imperial, Captain Miria Silverhand) Ginger (Unknown, Captain Lyra) Maui (300t Freighter, Captain Den) Scene summary: To avoid being detected, Klaiton pilots the Ginger using a gravity catapult, approaching in total silence (systems off) toward the tracker’s signal. After rounding the dark side of a moon, they discover the Mercy Future floating in the void, surrounded by a sea of space junk and the remains of gutted ships. They watch as the pirate ship dismantles the decoy shuttle. Den, commanding the Maui, begins his approach after picking up the crew members from the asteroid. The session ends with the crew frantically debating their next move: using the element of surprise to fry Miria with missiles, attempting a suicide boarding in combat suits, or contacting her to try to intimidate her and force her to surrender.

title: 67 - Once Eslavones
content: Session Summary: Negotiations in the Void and the Mystery of Ergo PCs present: Den, Daijiro, Lyra, Pika, Yaang-ki, Klaiton. (Jimmy is mentioned in a joke). NPCs present: Miria Silverhand, Mari Jagad (mentioned), Ferrik Redthane (mentioned), Petyr Vallis (mentioned). Key Developments The crew manages to resolve the threat of the pirate Miria Silverhand in the Hilfer system through diplomacy and bribery, avoiding direct combat and collecting the 50,000 credit bounty from the Belters.    They begin the expedition to the interdicted planet Ergo (under the control of the Third Imperium) to search for the crashed ship Stellar Osprey* using electronic warfare tactics to evade surveillance satellites.    After a grueling trek through the frozen mountains of Ergo, they locate the base camp of the Stellar Osprey* survivors, but discover that the original crew met a violent fate and that they are not alone in the mountains. Loose Ends Who was the mysterious figure riding a beast that watched them from the snowy peaks before disappearing?    What really happened at the Stellar Osprey* camp for the radio equipment to be destroyed with hammers and one of the crew members to end up with an ice axe in their brain? What radioactive liquid substance was the dead man handling before he died, considering his hands showed severe radiation burns? Session Joke The best joke came about when they were debating how to scan the surface of Ergo without having proper planetary probes or drones. Klaiton suggested tying Pika to a very long rope and hanging him below the atmosphere ("lowering him a little") with sensors on his fingertips and some "glass tupperware" that he would open and close to trap atmospheric samples, using him as a human probe. Scene 1: Planning and Fleet Distribution PCs present: Den, Daijiro, Lyra, Pika. NPCs present: None. (Gunners and pilots of the crew are mentioned). Location(s): Deep space. Ships mentioned: Maui (Freighter, Captain unspecified) Ginger (Freighter, Captain Lyra) Scene summary: The session begins with a meta-game debate that shifts into the narrative. Den expresses his frustration at the lack of action and his desire to take on a "bad pirate" role to speed things up after several weeks of commercial inactivity. Lyra, however, prefers to avoid the crew launching into a suicide mission without their main ship (the Banshee was destroyed previously). To resolve the imminent encounter, they decide to organize: Den and Yaang-ki stay on the Maui at a safe distance, while Lyra, Pika, Daijiro, and the rest of the main crew sneak in on the Ginger (with life support systems at minimum for four days) toward the target's position. Scene 2: From Pirate to Pirate PCs present: Lyra, Pika, Den, Daijiro, Klaiton. NPCs present: Miria Silverhand (Challenging, suspicious, tough negotiator; archetype: Veteran rival pirate), Mari Jagad (mentioned), Ferrik Redthane (mentioned), Petyr Vallis (mentioned). Location(s): Asteroid belt (Hilfer). Ships mentioned: Ginger (200-ton freighter, Captain Lyra) Mercyfish (400-ton ship, Captain Miria Silverhand) Scene summary: The Ginger locates the Mercyfish scrapping a water shuttle. Lyra opens communications with Captain Miria Silverhand, appearing relaxed but firm. Lyra warns her that the planet Hilfer is uniting against her and that the infamous bounty hunter Mari Jagad is in the system. Lyra proposes a "pirate to pirate" deal: if Miria leaves the system for a few weeks to let things cool down, they will share information on lucrative freighter routes in the future (offering a 60-40, then 50-50 split). Miria is skeptical and demands guarantees. Pika intervenes using his diplomatic skills and offers an advance of 75,000 credits (though due to a bad roll, this costs Pika a large portion of his personal savings). Miria agrees to leave and they agree to make contact again in 8 weeks. After Miria's departure, the Ginger's crew collects the 50,000 credit bounty from the local Belters for having resolved the problem. Scene 3: Infiltration of the Forbidden World PCs present: Pika, Lyra, Den, Yaang-ki, Klaiton, Daijiro. NPCs present: None. Location(s): Orbit and Gas Giant (Ergo System). Ships mentioned: Ginger (Freighter, Captain Lyra) Maui (Freighter, Captain unspecified) Scene summary: The crew prepares to travel to Ergo, a planet marked as a restricted zone by the Third Imperium. Before leaving, they buy a heavy "Hercules" tractor and a cargo crane that they install on the Ginger. After a week of travel through the Trojan Reach, they arrive in the system. They hide the Maui near a gas giant to refuel and the Ginger advances toward Ergo with transponders off. Pika uses electronic warfare to mask their signal and deceive the imperial satellites. They spend several days scanning the surface from orbit, discovering that Ergo is a living world with large agricultural operations, but also with ruins of radioactive cities. The coordinates that Daijiro provided point to a gigantic mountain range similar to the Himalayas, surrounded by perpetual storms. Scene 4: The Tempest and the Stellar Osprey PCs present: Klaiton, Lyra, Daijiro, Pika, Den, Yaang-ki. NPCs present: None alive (one corpse from the previous crew). Location(s): "Himalayan" mountain range (Ergo). Ships mentioned: Ginger (Freighter, Pilot Klaiton) Stellar Osprey (Crashed ship, Captain unknown) Scene summary: The crew equips themselves with environmental suits, cold-weather clothing, food for several days, and tents. Klaiton performs a masterful piloting maneuver through the hurricane-force winds of Ergo's atmosphere to drop the team off on a plateau, then retreats with the Ginger to a safe area. Daijiro takes on the role of guide and, with Lyra's help, leads an exhausting four-day march through erratic blizzards and deep snow.  Finally, they reach the coordinates and discover a calmer area where they dig up four sleds, frozen pack animals, and a collapsed tent. It belongs to the crew of the ship they are looking for: the Stellar Osprey. Inside the tent, they discover electronic equipment intentionally destroyed with hammers and the frozen corpse of a man with an ice axe stuck in his brain. Lyra's autopsy reveals that the man suffered from severe radiation burns on his hands before his murder. As they process the scene and try to find a trail toward the ship, a gust of wind clears their vision for a second, revealing a mysterious figure riding a beast watching them from the top of the rocks, which quickly disappears.

title: 68 - Tumba del Gavilan
content: The Secret of the Star Hawk PCs present: Den, Pika, Klaiton, Lyra, Yaang-ki, Daijiro NPCs present: KK11, Jim El Largo (referred to as Jim), Captain Chabán (mentioned) Major developments in the lives of the PCs or the long term campaign goal of rebuilding the Kingdom of Drinax: The crew has finally located the remains of the smuggler ship Star Hawk. Inside, they have discovered cargo of incalculable military and economic value: six intact Third Imperium-manufactured nuclear warheads. If they manage to extract them from Ergo and take them to Drinax, they will represent a massive resource for the reconstruction and defense of the Kingdom. Loose ends from the session that are unexplained or need to be followed up later in the campaign: How are they going to extract the six nuclear warheads from the crashed ship without cranes and with a perpetual storm? Where exactly is the Third Imperium underground facility on Ergo that is filled with the rest of the nuclear missiles? Who is the surveillance Type S Scout ship that is scanning Ergo's orbit and looking for the sabotaged satellites? What really happened to Jim El Largo’s mind after the radiation exposure or the events on Ergo?    Who is "Aparo," the mysterious and wealthy client who hired the Star Hawk* in the first place? Who were the natives (men and women dressed in furs) who lie dead from laser fire near the ship's camp? Session Joke: The best comedic moment of the session occurred during the tense negotiation with the security android KK11. While Den tried to apply pure logic and the Third Law of Robotics by demanding shelter for a wounded human, the stubborn robot simply pointed an integrated laser at his face and told him to get lost. Immediately after, Lyra requested an audience, and the security drone put her on hold with "elevator music." The mental image of Lyra wiggling and dancing to the rhythm of the little tune in the middle of a deadly blizzard, waiting for the killer robot to attend to her, caused the table to laugh. Scene 1: Links, Coordinates, and Passive Sensors PCs present: Klaiton, Lyra, Den, Yaang-ki, Daijiro, Pika NPCs present: None Place(s) and/or Planet(s): Camp in the mountain range and Orbit (Ergo) Spaceships: Jinger (Unknown model, Captain Lyra), Unknown Ship (Type S Scout model, unknown captain) Summary: The session begins with the crew analyzing a strange numerical poem recited by Jim El Largo. Klaiton deduces that the verses contain astrogation and piloting coordinates. However, communications between the ground team (sheltered in a tent in the middle of a snowstorm) and Klaiton (in orbit) are blocked by the electromagnetic field of Ergo's mountains. The situation gets tense when Klaiton detects an Imperial Type S Scout ship emerging in orbit and scanning the area. To avoid being discovered, Klaiton puts his ship in stealth mode and shuts down systems, leaving the ground team incommunicado and unaware of the orbital danger. Scene 2: The Infernal Ascent PCs present: Lyra, Den, Yaang-ki, Daijiro, Pika NPCs present: None Place(s) and/or Planet(s): Mountain Range (Ergo) Spaceships: None Summary: Given the lack of communications, the ground team decides to follow the ascending path in search of the Star Hawk. The climb is brutal; the extreme cold and hurricane-force winds push the group's physical endurance to the limit. Pika suffers especially from the ravages of the climate, failing almost all of her stamina checks and being on the verge of collapsing, but Den manages to keep her on her feet by injecting her with stimulants. After a day of exhausting travel, the path descends toward a small, sheltered valley where they finally spot a severely damaged Type S Scout ship that is melting snow to power its reactor. Scene 3: Negotiations with KK11 PCs present: Den, Lyra, Yaang-ki, Daijiro, Pika NPCs present: KK11 (Android with a circle of sensors for a face and integrated weapons. Wears the tarnished rags of a crew uniform. Archetype: The stoic and stubborn watchdog, tied to his last orders). Place(s) and/or Planet(s): Crash Valley (Ergo) Spaceships: Star Hawk (Type S Scout, Captain Chabán) Summary: The team approaches cautiously. Den steps forward with his hands raised to parley, but is intercepted by a security drone and, subsequently, by KK11, who aims a laser at him. Den tries to reason with the machine by appealing to its programming and medical necessity, but the robot refuses to let them in, stating that it is awaiting the return of Captain Chabán and First Officer Jim, who have been gone for more than 11 years. Den withdraws, annoyed. Lyra takes over, using diplomacy, reciting Jim’s poem to the machine and pretending to be a rescue team sent by him. KK11 lowers the weapon, accepts the "code," and allows Lyra to enter the ship for a damage assessment. Meanwhile, Den discovers several corpses of Ergo natives under the snow, murdered by laser shots to the back. Scene 4: The Logbook and the Secret of Ergo PCs present: Lyra, Yaang-ki, Pika NPCs present: KK11 Place(s) and/or Planet(s): Interior of the Star Hawk (Ergo) Spaceships: Star Hawk (Type S Scout, Captain Chabán) Summary: Dressed in a vac-suit to protect herself from a radioactive leak from the reactor, Lyra enters the ship escorted by KK11. The android gives her a bleak damage report: the jump drive is destroyed, the sensors are melted, and the hull is compromised, although the missile turret works. In the cargo hold, Lyra discovers the true cargo that the robot is guarding: six Third Imperium nuclear warheads. While Lyra distracts KK11 by ordering it to evaluate the ship, Yaang-ki puts on a vac-suit and, with the remote help of Pika’s software, manages to hack the ship's computer after several days of work. They extract the logbook, revealing that Captain Chabán and Jim were hired in Szirp by someone named "Aparo." Upon arriving on Ergo, they discovered not only secret luxury villas on a theoretically dead world, but an underground warehouse full of Imperial nuclear bombs. After stealing several to sell them, they were shot down by orbital security, which caused the accident, the captain’s death, Jim’s madness, and left KK11 jealously guarding the missiles in the frozen valley. The crew now debates how to dismantle the valuable parts of the ship and take the nuclear warheads.

title: 69 - Chatarreros
content: Session Summary: Looting on the Ice and Flight from Ergo PCs present: Pika, Lyra, Daijiro, Den, Klaiton. NPCs present: Krrsh, Yaang-ki. (Mentioned: Thao Poloc, Eihei the Wise, King Oleb, Miria). Main developments or campaign goals: The group has successfully dismantled and looted the most valuable components of the crashed ship Gavilán (engines, power plant, sensors, computers, turret, etc.), securing loot valued at about 10 million credits that will greatly assist in financing the reconstruction of the Kingdom of Drinax or upgrading their own fleet. Additionally, they managed to decipher the landing instructions hidden in the song of Eihei the Wise so that the Ginger could land on the planet. Loose ends: Six imperial tactical nuclear warheads have been left behind in a silo or hidden base on Ergo due to a lack of equipment and time to transport them. An unknown, fast ship (200 tons, Thrust 6) has taken off from Ergo and is pursuing them just as they attempt to leave the atmosphere. Who is piloting it and what are their intentions? The nature and exact origin of the hostile natives inhabiting the ravines of Ergo remain a mystery. They have a pending meeting with the pirate Miria on Keiteroa, for which they might be late. Joke of the Session: The best comedic moment of the session occurred when the players put maximum effort into crafting an incredibly dramatic and emotional speech to convince the robot Krrsh that its captain, Thao Poloc, had died tragically in the snow and had delegated the mission of taking the cargo to them. After the intense performance and a failed roll, the game master described how the robot simply drew its weapon and said coldly: "Just what a thief would say." (Honorable mention to the suggestion of gifting an atomic bomb to King Oleb as if it were an engagement ring). Scene 1: The Diagnosis of the Gavilán and the Failed Negotiation PCs present: Pika, Lyra, Daijiro, Klaiton. NPCs present: Krrsh (Mechanical robot model KK-11, armed with a laser pistol and mechanical arm. Logical, stubborn, and strict with its orders - Archetype: Incorruptible Guardian / Rigid Machine). Thao Poloc (Mentioned). Location: Frozen valley, next to the Gavilán (Ergo). Ships mentioned: Gavilán (Type S Scout Model, Captain Thao Poloc), Ginger (Injenior Jet Model). Scene summary: Pika finishes analyzing the Gavilán and discovers that the ship is practically destroyed: the jump drive is junk, the power plant has radiation leaks, and the hull is half-buried in ice. They conclude that repairing it is a money pit and decide it is better to loot its valuable components. To avoid a conflict, Klaiton and Pika try to convince the guardian robot, Krrsh, that its former captain, Thao Poloc, died tragically in Cordán due to the cold and passed the mission of safeguarding the cargo to them. Despite the elaborate and emotional speech, Krrsh's circuits detect the deception, it labels their words as those of thieves, and draws its weapon, initiating combat. Scene 2: Blood and Lasers in the Cargo Hold PCs present: Pika, Lyra, Daijiro, Den. NPCs present: Krrsh (Damaged and smoking after the combat - Archetype: Incorruptible Guardian), Security Drone (Flying drone, equipped with laser and stunner, agile - Archetype: Mindless Killing Machine). Location: Cargo hold of the Gavilán (Ergo). Ships mentioned: Gavilán (Type S Scout Model). Scene summary: A brutal shootout breaks out inside the ship. Krrsh fires at point-blank range at Daijiro, wounding him seriously in the chest, but the swordsman manages to get close and dismember the robot with his static sword, tearing it to pieces. However, a hidden security drone joins the fray, flying over the nuclear warheads and unleashing a rain of laser fire and stun shots. Den is seriously wounded and Daijiro is forced to use an aerosol grenade to create a reflective cloud to dissipate the lasers. Lyra tries to provide covering fire (almost accidentally shooting a nuclear warhead) and provides medical equipment. Finally, after exchanging multiple shots, Den and Pika manage to take down the drone. Once the area is secured, they heal Daijiro's wounds and Pika collects Krrsh's mechanical parts with the hope of reprogramming it in the future. Scene 3: Ambush in the Ravine PCs present: Lyra, Den, Pika. NPCs present: Hostile natives (Young men, but hardened by the cold, with frostbite amputations, dressed in furs, armed with bows, spears, and rudimentary metal axes - Archetype: Savage Hunters/Extreme Survivors). Location: Mountain ravine and Base Camp (Ergo). Ships mentioned: None. Scene summary: Lyra, Den, and Pika undertake a hard journey back to base camp through the snowy ravines to try to communicate with their ship without being blocked by the valley's radiation. In the middle of a blizzard, they are ambushed by four hostile natives. Two of them attack with bows from elevated positions, while another two charge melee against Den with spears and large axes. Despite receiving a heavy axe blow that dents his armor, Den draws his official pistol and takes down the two melee attackers with lethal shots. Lyra, seeking cover, manages to land a precise shot on the foot of one of the archers, making him fall down the rocks. The last native flees into the storm. After a quick search of the corpses, in which they only find dried meat, the group continues until they take refuge in the old base camp. Scene 4: Blind Landing and Desperate Escape PCs present: Lyra, Klaiton, Pika, Den, Daijiro. NPCs present: Yaang-ki (Quiet and willing to help with the dismantling - Archetype: Support Companion). Eihei the Wise (Mentioned). Miria (Mentioned). Location: Base Camp, Frozen Valley, and Orbit (Ergo). Ships mentioned: Ginger (Injenior Jet Model, piloted by Klaiton), Gavilán (Type S Scout Model), Maui (Gunship with civilian sensors, hidden in a gas giant), Unknown ship (200 tons, Thrust 6). Scene summary: From the base camp, Lyra manages to establish precarious communication with Klaiton, who is waiting in orbit aboard the Ginger, and transmits the flight codes hidden in the song of Eihei the Wise. Guiding himself only by a compass and a barometer, Klaiton performs a risky atmospheric reentry maneuver, managing to land the Ginger in the valley with only a few scratches on the hull. During the next two weeks, the team works feverishly dismantling the power plant, engines, turret, and computers of the Gavilán, filling the 55 tons of cargo capacity of their ship, although they decide to leave the nuclear warheads behind to avoid risks and delays. With provisions at their limit and knowing their position has been betrayed, they take off at full power toward space. As soon as they leave the atmosphere, the sensors detect a fast 200-ton imperial ship that has taken off after them and is heading to intercept them at maximum speed.

title: 70 - Corre como puedas
content: Escape in extremis to Hilfer PCs present: Den, Pika, Klaiton, Lyra, Daijiro, Yaang-ki. NPCs present: None physically in the scenes, but Miria Silverhand, Krrsh, and First Officer Mari Jagad are actively discussed and mentioned in the final planning. Main developments in the campaign (Rebuilding the Kingdom of Drinax): The characters manage to secure the valuable technological and military loot from the Star Hawk (including six nuclear warheads and high-value components). Despite their ship being nearly destroyed in the process, the crew establishes a logistical plan to split up: they will strengthen their diplomatic ties by delivering a power plant in Kteiroa, upgrade their military fleet (transferring military sensors to their main ship), and plot a trade route to Theev, where the nuclear warheads could finance a large portion of their future pirate and diplomatic efforts. Loose ends: The pending appointment with the pirate Miria Silverhand, who may grow impatient at the group's delay.  The complete structural repair of the ship Ginger*, which requires a dry dock or shipyard due to the massive damage received. The safe transport of the nuclear warheads to Theev without being intercepted. Recovering part of the cargo that was lost during the bridge decompression following the attack. Session joke: The best comedic moment occurs at the height of the space combat. The ship is taking critical hits, there is fire, sparks, loss of oxygen, and Klaiton curses while struggling with the engines. While everyone panics taking on crucial roles, Daijiro (whose piloting and engineering skills are nil) puts on his vacuum suit and, with total composure, announces that he is placing his "skills" at the disposal of the captains: he offers to prepare tea, coffee, or dinner, justifying that "otherwise, I would have starved to death." The absurd calmness and futility of his contribution in the midst of imminent destruction sets off the group's laughter. Scene 1: Ambush in orbit PCs present: Den, Pika, Klaiton, Lyra, Daijiro, Yaang-ki. NPCs present: None. Location(s) / Planet(s): Orbit of Ergo (Deep Space). Ships mentioned: Ginger (PC ship, 200 tons), Maui (PC ship, 400 tons, out of visual range), enemy System Defense Ship (military ship, 200 tons). Summary of the scene: Barely 15 minutes after leaving the atmosphere and loaded with the loot and nuclear warheads extracted from the Star Hawk, the Ginger's scanners detect a system defense ship approaching at maximum power. The crew panics upon noticing that their other ship, the Maui, is hours away and communications are jammed. They quickly take their stations: Klaiton to engineering, Lyra to sensors and electronic warfare, Den and Yaang-ki to the double pulse laser turrets, and Pika to try to calculate an emergency jump. The enemy launches multiple missile salvos. Although Yaang-ki manages to destroy one with defensive fire, two missiles impact the Ginger violently, causing 22 points of damage, breaching the armor, causing a serious fuel leak, and damaging the maneuver drive. Scene 2: Jumping to pieces PCs present: Den, Pika, Klaiton, Lyra, Daijiro, Yaang-ki. NPCs present: None. Location(s) / Planet(s): Orbit of Ergo (Near space). Ships mentioned: Ginger, enemy System Defense Ship. Summary of the scene: The enemy ship closes the distance and fires a devastating point-blank burst with beam lasers and more missiles. Den and Yaang-ki manage to destroy the new missile salvo at the last second, but the lasers pierce the Ginger's hull. They suffer another 10 points of damage and several critical hits that destroy life support and volatilize part of the cargo (the computers they had just looted). Alarms sound and the crew runs out of oxygen, relying on their vacuum suits. Pika fails to plot a clear jump route. In a desperate moment, Lyra uses psychological techniques learned in the Silent Hand to calm Klaiton and induce him into a trance of concentration. Smoking his last "Blue" brand cigar, Klaiton manages to engage the jump drive, overcoming Ergo's massive gravitational interference. The Ginger jumps into hyperspace a moment before being annihilated. Scene 3: Repairs in the dark PCs present: Den, Pika, Klaiton, Lyra, Daijiro, Yaang-ki. NPCs present: None. Location(s) / Planet(s): Hyperspace. Ships mentioned: Ginger. Summary of the scene: Once in hyperspace, the initial euphoria of having survived fades while reviewing the damage. The greatest danger is the fuel leak, which threatens to leave them stranded in the void. The crew spends the jump week working against the clock. Lyra and Pika combine their technical knowledge and manage to seal the fuel leak, consuming most of their valuable tons of spare parts. Fortunately, the life support system manages to be repaired without requiring additional materials ("putting a screw back in its place"). During this time, they realize the nuclear warheads remain intact despite the destruction of the rest of the cargo. Scene 4: Arrival at Hilfer and the pirate council PCs present: Den, Pika, Klaiton, Lyra, Daijiro, Yaang-ki. NPCs present: Miria Silverhand (Impatient pirate, mentioned), Krrsh (Mentioned), Mari Jagad (Mentioned). Location(s) / Planet(s): Hilfer, Kteiroa, Theev (Mentioned as destinations), Marduk, Borite, Noricum, Palindrome (Mentioned in the route). Ships mentioned: Ginger, Maui, Star Hawk (wrecks mentioned), Banshee (Mentioned as a desired purchase), Corsair (Pirate ship, mentioned as a target). Summary of the scene: The Ginger exits hyperspace in the Hilfer system with fuel at critical levels. They are assisted by local belters (to whom they cover up the truth by saying they were attacked by pirates) and manage to refuel. A couple of days later, the majestic Maui arrives in the system, confirming they managed to pick up Pika's message. Now safe, the group debates the strategy to follow. They have too much loot and urgent missions. They decide to split the crew and their assets: Lyra and Pika will stay in Hilfer along with the Maui to try to sell scrap, buy necessary pipes, and transfer the Star Hawk's advanced military sensors to the ship. Meanwhile, Den, Klaiton, Yaang-ki, and Daijiro will take the battered Ginger toward Kteiroa to deliver the promised power plant and gain allies. They leave for the immediate future the trip to distant Theev (where they hope to sell the nuclear warheads for millions) and the tense meeting agreed upon with Miria Silverhand, fantasizing before saying goodbye about stealing or buying a fearsome Corsair in the future.

title: 71 - Plata, Leones y Pantanos
content: Session Summary: Business, Aslan, and a Swamp Monastery PCs present: Den (also playing as Fénix), Pika, Klaiton, Lyra, Yaang-ki, Daijiro. NPCs present/mentioned: Miria Silverhand, Petyr Vallis, Kasiyl, Eihei the Wise, Fyukh, Krrsh. Utea and Io Drocles also appear (mentioned in the transcript). Key character or campaign developments (Rebuilding the Kingdom of Drinax): The crew has managed to repair severe structural damage to the Ginger and upgraded the Maui by installing an onboard workshop. Politically and commercially, they have managed to establish an excellent diplomatic relationship with the Aslan matriarch Utea in Kteiroa, selling her vital machinery. This secures them a safe and allied port on the borders of the Hierate, very close to Drinax, thus fulfilling a major goal of expanding their influence. Additionally, they have resumed active piracy by allying with Miria Silverhand to successfully raid a Floriani League freighter. Loose ends: Pika's contact in the Hilfer underworld remains active and could provide more targets in the future. The Floriani League has been attacked. After the assault, the crew had the feeling that "they took note of our registration," so they could suffer reprisals. The Ihatei faction has fragmented; some have gone to Fantasy and others work as mercenaries in Tyr. Their threat to Drinax has paused, but not completely eliminated.  It remains to be decided what the crew's next major destination will be (they are hesitating between traveling to Cordan or toward the Sindalian Main). Den (Fénix) continues to yearn for a ship on par with his old Banshee*. Joke of the Session: The "Litter Box Incident." While Den was trying to negotiate over the radio with an Aslan warship, he tried to explain that they were carrying a recycling plant to help clean up the colony. His choice of words ("so we can filter all the poop, all your excrement") was a diplomatic disaster. Daijiro caused laughter at the table by pointing out the glaring mistake: they had just told a race of proud warrior felines how to manage their toilets, forgetting that, being cats, "they poop in the litter box." This provoked a tense, immediate boarding. Scene 1: Market, Repairs, and Scrap PCs present: Lyra, Yaang-ki, Daijiro, Pika, Klaiton, Den. NPCs present: KK11 (Broken). Location: Spaceport (Hilfer / Hilfer System). Ships mentioned: Ginger (Corsair, Captain Lyra / Fénix) Maui (300t freighter, Captain Pika) Gavilán (Mentioned for scrapping) Summary: The crew is in Hilfer licking their wounds. The Ginger is severely damaged and the robot KK11 is destroyed. They spend several weeks managing their resources. Lyra and Yaang-ki go down to the market (which does not yet have a computerized Agora system) to sell engines and fuel processors, managing an excellent deal that earns them over 2 million credits. With that money, they buy 40 tons of pipes and spare parts. Meanwhile, Yaang-ki, Daijiro, Klaiton, and Den get their hands dirty repairing critical hull and cargo bay impacts on the Ginger, as well as fixing the maneuver drive. For his part, Pika spends the time installing a full workshop in the Maui’s hold for future repairs. Scene 2: Feline Diplomacy in the Frontiers PCs present: Pika, Klaiton, Den (as Fénix), Daijiro. NPCs present: Utea (Old Aslan matriarch, dull fur, wrapped in fur coats - Archetype: Cunning and pragmatic clan leader). Aslan Captain (Young, large, with ceremonial axe and combat armor - Archetype: Proud warrior). Eihei the Wise and Fyukh (Mentioned when discussing Ihatei politics). Location: Spaceport / Camp (Kteiroa / Kteiroa System). Previous refueling stop in (Pourne). Ships mentioned: Ginger (Corsair, Captain Fénix) Argos (Type S Scout, Captain Io Drocles) Summary: The Ginger, escorted by the messenger Io Drocles in the Argos, jumps toward Kteiroa after refueling in Pourne. Upon arrival, they discover that the system is teeming with Aslan civilian and military ships. After Pika's comical diplomatic error over the radio, they are boarded by a group of Aslan warriors. Daijiro manages to earn the respect of the leader's young son through warrior body language, complimenting his axe. Once at the spaceport, Fénix meets with the matriarch Utea. They deliver the valuable recycling and energy machinery, collecting 400,000 credits. Most importantly, they secure an alliance; Utea guarantees them free entry into her territory and updates them on Aslan politics: the Ihatei have lost strength after their failure in Drinax, scattering toward Fantasy or as mercenaries in Tyr. Scene 3: Quick Hit on the Florians PCs present: Lyra, Pika. NPCs present: Miria Silverhand (Confident, aggressive - Archetype: Bloodthirsty veteran pirate). Location: Orbit / Deep Space (Hilfer System). Ships mentioned: Maui (300t freighter, Captain Pika) Mercifuge (Corsair ship, Captain Miria Silverhand) Floriani League ship (Large tonnage independent freighter) Summary: Thanks to Lyra's contact in Hilfer, they learn that a valuable independent freighter is about to set sail. The Maui meets in deep space with Miria Silverhand's Mercifuge. Lyra takes tactical command of the assault. They agree to strike hard and fast before the ship can call for help. The maneuver is a resounding success: they board the ship (identified as belonging to the Floriani League) and in a lightning strike manage to steal cargo worth 240,000 credits. They flee quickly before the system patrols arrive, albeit with the unsettling feeling that the strange Floriani crew members have memorized who they are. Scene 4: Retreat in the Swamp PCs present: Lyra, Pika, Den, Yaang-ki, Daijiro, Klaiton. NPCs present: Miria Silverhand (Archetype: Bloodthirsty veteran pirate). Location: Swamp / Monastery / Class D Spaceport (Sink / Sink System). Ships mentioned: Maui (300t freighter, Captain Pika) Ginger (Corsair, Captain Fénix) Mercifuge (Corsair ship, Captain Miria Silverhand) Summary: After the successful robbery, the Maui escapes by jumping to Sink, an inhospitable swamp planet. Upon landing in the mud, they discover that the only population are outcasts from the Third Empire and a strange sect of about 800 barefoot and shaven monks who live in a stone monastery. These monks worship the lakes, believe that water is intelligent, and practice ritual drownings. Miria Silverhand meets with them, takes her 40,000 credits as her share of the loot, and says goodbye, announcing that she is heading toward the Sindalian Main for a change of scenery. Days later, the Ginger arrives at Sink, reuniting the entire crew. They spend the weeks studying, training new skills, and debating their next move: hesitating whether to travel to Cordan to attend to noble affairs, or to continue pirating to heavily arm the Maui.
